title: The Miracle Sudoku Reborn
description:
*** Today's Sudoku ***

Doesn't this puzzle look familiar?  In fact it's got the exact same digits in the exact same positions as Mitchell Lee's Miracle Sudoku from May 2020.  But Mátyás Martinka has reinvented the puzzle by tweaking its ruleset!  We don't know if it's easier or harder now but it's definitely interesting!! Play the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/2ftJ4jLbDG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's or king's move in chess cannot contain the same digit. Digits in the Nth column indicate in which column the digit N is placed in the respective row. Eg if R3C2 is a 5, the fifth column in the third row (R3C5) must contain a 2.

title: A Festive Gas Burst!
description:

Normal Sudoku rules apply. If a clue is given outside the grid, then there must be three consecutive cells somewhere in that row or column which sum to the clue value
GAS 182 – The Letter K by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/2p8m5nkb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line must have values strictly between the values in the circles on the ends of that line.

Normal sudoku rules apply. The small digit in the top left corner of a cage is either the correct digit that goes in that cell, or it is one higher or one lower than the correct digit.

title: The Sudoku Grid(iron)
description:
Here's where you can play Sudoku Bowl by apetersen: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rqGH96246T 
The players (open circles) will run their assigned routes and blocking schemes (arrows). To run the routes correctly, the digits along the arrows must sum to the number in the circle.
The endzone (row 1) will be painted in alternating colors (of your choosing: the grey circles hold odd numbers; the grey squares hold even numbers.)
There was a penalty flag thrown on the previous play (the X). It was a 10 yard penalty (meaning the 2 digits surrounding the X must sum to 10).
Normal sudoku rules apply.

title: A Gorgeous Christmas Tree
description:
Merry Christmas! Here is where you can try Walking Writer's Christmas Tree: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6pQgD6jgJn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along the green Christmas tree line alternate between odd and even numbers. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in the connecting circle. (The bottom two arrows represent garland and the top arrow is a star.) Digits connected by a white Kropki dot must be consecutive. (These represent tree lights.) The digit in the large quadruple circle must be in at least one of the four connecting cells. (This represents a large ornament.) And the gray square at the base of the tree is an even digit. (This represents the tree stand.)

title: A Rat Celebrates Christmas
description:
Here's where you can try A Part Ridge and a Pair of 3s by Dittman Rat: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gjQ8Fhjnbg 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat on the marked diagonal. The 7 grey cells are a "ridge" of high numbers parting the two sides of the grid, meaning each digit in a grey cell must be larger than the digits in white cells which share an edge. One of the four pairs of coloured boxes contains two 3s. None of the other coloured boxes may contain any 3s.

title: CtC: The Christmas Movie
description:
*** Our Christmas Gift ***

To all our patrons - thank you so much for your support.  

We are delighted to bring you a fantastic Christmas present - a puzzle/sudoku hunt by some wonderful constructors: PjotrV, Panthera and Aspartagcus.  You can access the hunt here (the password is on Patreon right now):

https://amgine.nl 

Enjoy - and please do try to still see your families over the holidays - we know these puzzles are addictive :)

*** Today's Sudoku ***

Ok, you all said you wanted to see one of us really struggle...  Tallcat obliges with his Read Between The Lines sudoku which is a bit of a beast but it thoroughly beats Simon up! Give it a go at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mqBfrp8gGh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Circles represent one end of a "Between Line". Circle digits give the length of the rest of the line including line cells and the other endpoint (eg 3 = 2 line cells + the other endpoint cell). Other endpoints are not circled digits. Line digits must have a value between the two endpoint digits. Lines may only move orthogonally, cannot cross or share endpoints. All Between Lines have at least one line cell. Endpoints of the same Between Line may not be in orthogonally adjacent cells.

If you are unsure how the rules ought to work then there is an example here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0008F4

123
456
789

title: Solve A Classic Riddle Using A Sudoku!
description:
*** Our Christmas Gift ***

To all our patrons - thank you so much for your support.  

We are delighted to bring you a fantastic Christmas present - a puzzle/sudoku hunt by some wonderful constructors: PjotrV, Panthera and Aspartagcus.  You can access the hunt here (the password is on Patreon right now):

https://amgine.nl 

Enjoy - and please do try to still see your families over the holidays - we know these puzzles are addictive :)

*** Today's Sudoku ***

The latest in ZegreS' magnificent Sudoku Riddle series today!  30 Zombies in 20 minutes is another stunner although, for some reason, it reminds Simon of U2...  Give it a go at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/nFHGGRm34m

Riddle
On a dark, moonless night, four friends are escaping a horde of 30 zombies. They come to an old rickety bridge. At most two can cross the bridge at a time and they must use a flashlight to see. They only have one flashlight, so someone must bring it back each time until everyone is across. Shaun takes 1 minute to cross, Liz takes 3, Ed takes 7 and Dianne takes 9. The zombies will get to the bridge in 20 minutes. How can everyone get across before the zombies arrive? 

Sudoku rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Digits on indicated diagonals sum to the pointing value. Rows 1,3,5,7,9 represent bridge crossings in order. The friends have to get from the left bank to the right. Place them on the bridge (ie the arrow) and the banks on either side. People are represented by their crossing time. The sandwich clues to the right indicate the total time after each crossing. A sandwich clue gives the sum of digits "sandwiched" between the 1 and 9 in their row.

title: GAS On, GAS Off
description:
Here are the URLs for GAS puzzles 171-175:
GAS 171 – Quad Max by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/b2vu85wp 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Arrows point to the largest digit in the four surrounding cells, which must appear only once in those four cells. Smaller digits may be repeated. 
GAS 172 – Easy as 1,2,3 by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://tinyurl.com/25kkcrfn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 173 Summoning Baphomet by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/yc34zmun 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A value in a white circle shows the largest digit that appears in the four cells surrounding that circle. (Digits around a white circle with a value, including the largest value, may repeat as long as they follow sudoku rules.) An arrow in a white circle points to the uniquely largest digit in the four cells surrounding it. (Smaller digits may repeat as long as they follow sudoku rules, but the largest digit must only appear in the cell pointed to by the arrow.)
GAS 174 – Thermo by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/mshjcs58 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer must strictly increase, starting at the round bulb (but are not necessarily consecutive!).
GAS 175 – Irregular Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://tinyurl.com/4vfdtwam 
Place a digit from 1-9 into each empty cell so that every row, column and bold outlined region contains each digit exactly once.

title: Solve More Pencil Puzzles With Me
description:
Today Simon turns again to the Genuinely Approachable Pencil Puzzles published on the new channel "Daily Pencil Puzzle Discussion" on the Cracking The Cryptic Fan Discord server.  This channel publishes one new puzzle every day and they are an absolute treat.  You can join the Discord server here:
https://discord.gg/BbN89j5

If you do enjoy this video there is another with eight different puzzles available right now for our patrons on Patreon:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

and also two more videos like this one, which are on the channel already here:
https://youtu.be/fzS99RfGy8I
https://youtu.be/Ij-n1AFh3ug

Unequal Length Maze by Eric Fox

Draw a non-intersecting path through the centers of all empty cells, starting from the S (start) and finishing at the G (goal). No two consecutive straight lines in the path may be of the same length.

https://tinyurl.com/pw63xfe3

Rectangle Slider by shye

Move some black squares (1x1's, and not necessarily all of them) so that each group of orthogonally adjacent squares is rectangular in shape, and no square is left isolated as a 1x1. A square may only move in one straight line vertically or horizontally. Squares’ paths may not cross each other, other squares, or other squares’ starting points. Squares containing clues must be moved exactly the indicated number of cells.

https://tinyurl.com/2p9herhw

Double Back by jovi_al

Draw a non-intersecting, non-branching loop through the centers of all cells which passes through each region exactly twice.

https://tinyurl.com/4v5h3y2p

Bosnian Road by Tygrannus

Shade cells in the grid that form a single closed, non-branching loop that cannot touch itself, not even diagonally. Number clues are always unshaded and indicate how many shaded cells it sees orthogonally and diagonally from 1-8 (like minesweeper).

https://tinyurl.com/2p8pyr59

Sashigane by Freddie Hand

Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells. Each region must be an L shape with a width of one cell. Arrows must lie at one end of an L and point toward the bend. Circles must lie at the bend of an L, and if one contains a number, the L it’s inside must contain the indicated amount of cells.

https://tinyurl.com/2p994a3u

LITS by Eric Fox

Shade one tetromino of cells in each region so that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Two tetrominoes of the same shape may not share a bold border, counting rotations and reflections as the same. No 2x2 region may be entirely shaded.

https://tinyurl.com/h5832vyx

Cave by shye

Shade some cells so that the shaded cells are all connected orthogonally by other shaded cells to the edge of the grid, and the remaining unshaded cells form one orthogonally connected area, the cave. Clues cannot be shaded, and represent the total number of unshaded cells that can be seen in a straight line vertically or horizontally, including the cell itself.

https://tinyurl.com/2p9cr2tn

Shikaku by jovi_al

Divide the entire grid into rectangular regions, each containing exactly one circle. A number inside a circle indicates the number of cells in its rectangle.

https://tinyurl.com/yz82wrt4

title: More GAS, More Glory
description:
Here's where you can try today's 5 days of GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles (actually nos 166-170, despite the title card in the video!):
GAS 166 – A Trio of Trios by Sam Cappleman-Lynes across three pages: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rNFffthDhj 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bMtQ29Qq7D   https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/G7MfBMnB8h 
Or try them together on Penpa: https://git.io/J1KYQ 
1-6 must appear in each row, column and box. Digits along an arrow sum to the number in the circle. Digits in a cage must not repeat, and sum to the total given. Digits on a marked diagonal must not repeat. If two cells in any two grids have the same letter written in them, those cells must contain the same digit.
GAS 167 – Return of the Clones by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/v844n3ee 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Blue regions are clones, and must contain the same digits in the same relative positions. Digits along thermometers must strictly increase from bulb to tip.
GAS 168 – Irregular Frame by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/sp3s343d 
Each row, column, and marked 9-cell region must contain the digits 1 through 9 once each. A value outside of the grid tells you the sum of all of the digits up to the first region border. For instance, the '9' above the rightmost column tells you that the topmost three digits in that column sum to 9.
GAS 169 – Answer Eight by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://tinyurl.com/4s4h555v 
ormal Sudoku rules apply. If two cells are separated by a grey dot then the digits they contain must be able to produce the answer 8 by applying one of the four standard arithmetic operations. If two cells are not separated by a dot then this may or may not be the case.
GAS 170 – Thing of Shapes by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/z3ce74mc 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must strictly increase from bulb to tip. Digits cannot repeat on the marked diagonals.

At the very end of this video Simon, who is somewhat traumatised by this point as you can see, spies a 4 in r9c4 and thinks "negative constraint" as a way of disambiguating the final pattern. title: Learn To Play Pencil Puzzles
description:
Today Simon turns again to the Genuinely Approachable Pencil Puzzles published on the new channel "Daily Pencil Puzzle Discussion" on the Cracking The Cryptic Fan Discord server.  This channel publishes one new puzzle every day and they are an absolute treat.  You can join the Discord server here:
https://discord.gg/BbN89j5

If you do enjoy this video there is another with eight different puzzles available right now for our patrons on Patreon:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

and also another video like this one, which is on the channel already here:
https://youtu.be/fzS99RfGy8I

Puzzle 1: Yajilin by jovi_al

https://tinyurl.com/2p872bc8

Rules: Shade some cells so that no two shaded cells are orthogonally adjacent and draw a non-intersecting loop through the centers of all of the remaining empty cells. Clues cannot be shaded, and represent the number of shaded cells in a straight line in the indicated direction between the clue and the border of the puzzle (i.e. clues see through each other). You may place shaded cells that do not directly see or interfere with any of the clues.

Puzzle 2: Slant by Tyrgannus

https://tinyurl.com/2p8u8t6t 

Rules: Draw a diagonal line in each cell that connects the opposite corners of that cell. Diagonal lines cannot form closed loops within the puzzle. Numbered clues show how many lines are extending from that circle. Note that EVERY cell must have a diagonal line through it.

Puzzle 3: Easy as ABC by Freddie Hand 

https://tinyurl.com/5dv2456m 

Rules: Place letters from the range given outside the grid (A-C in this case) into some cells so that each row and column contains each letter once. A clue outside the grid represents the first letter seen in the corresponding row or column from that direction.

Puzzle 4: Voxas by Eric Fox

https://tinyurl.com/5fuvrxe9 

Rules: Divide the grid into 1x2 and 1x3 regions. Borders must separate two different regions. Borders with white dots separate regions with the same size and orientation. Borders with black dots separate regions with neither the same size nor the same orientation. Borders with grey dots separate regions with either the same size or the same orientation, but not both.

Puzzle 5: Compass by shye 

https://tinyurl.com/yckhh5ys 

Rules: Divide the grid into regions of orthogonally connected cells, each containing exactly one compass. A number in a compass indicates how many cells belong to its region that are further in the indicated direction than the compass itself.

Puzzle 6: Moon or Sun by jovi_al

https://tinyurl.com/ycknejry 

Rules: Draw a non-intersecting, non-branching loop through the centers of some cells which enters and exits each region exactly once. Within a region, the loop must pass through all moons and no suns, or all suns and no moons. The loop may not pass through the same type of clue in two consecutively used regions.

Puzzle 7: Nurikabe by Tyrgannus 

https://tinyurl.com/2vjpwjt5 

Rules: Shade cells in the puzzle where all shaded cells are orthogonally connected but never form a 2x2 shaded region. Number clues are never shaded and show the number of orthogonally connected unshaded cells it is part of. All unshaded areas are clued.

Puzzle 8: Meandering Numbers by Freddie Hand

https://tinyurl.com/2p88bnu5

Rules: Place a number into each cell so that each region contains an orthogonally-connected chain of consecutive numbers from 1 to N, where N is the number of cells in the region. Numbers of the same value may not touch one another, not even diagonally.

title: Where In The World Is This Sudoku From?
description:
*** Today's Sudoku***

And now for something a bit different!  Today's puzzle, which is by Hraf, uses the real geography of the Wirral Peninsula in just a wonderful sudoku that's dedicated to Hraf's grandparents:

"This puzzle is dedicated to my grandparents who are from Liverpool:
My grandfather, who passed earlier this year; but especially to my
grandmother, who taught me from a young age to love puzzles and encouraged my curiosity about the world."

You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GMmTTqFhp2

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The blue areas represent the water surrounding the Wirral Peninsula. The green areas are land. On land, the digit in a cell represents the height of a skyscraper built in that cell. No skyscrapers can be built on water, so any digit can appear on water without affecting sightlines. Sightlines to a shorter building are blocked by taller buildings. The cages represent places where photographs were taken by a photographer on a boat cruise. The small arrow in a cage represents the direction the photographer was facing. Additionally, the digit given in the cage represents the number of skyscrapers visible in the given direction. In places where multiple photographs were taken, all of the photographs will be clued in the same cage. The digit in the cell with a grey square is even. Note: Because no skyscrapers are built on water, no digits in those cells block sightline to any land which may be across the water from the photographer.

title: Lady Or The Tiger: The Classic Riddle
description:
*** Today's Sudoku***

We love innovations in sudoku and ZegreS' idea to make sudokus that are hybrids with famous riddles tickles us pink.  We did one of these a couple of weeks ago and here's another one!  This time it borrows from a famous riddle in The Lady Or The Tiger by Raymond Smullyan.  Who would be the reward behind the door if you had a choice?  If we get enough replies we'll reveal our most desired party guests X)

You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6nb6Ndf63L

Rules: 
Riddle part:
A lovably eccentric king has put before you a test. Choose one of three doors and encounter either: a lady (represented by the digit 1) who is the life and soul of a party or a tiger (represented by the digit 9) struggling with intermittent fasting. Behind two doors (in the cage) is a tiger (9) and no lady (1). Behind one door (in the cage) is a lady (1) and no tiger (9).  Signs hang above each door: Above Room 1: A tiger is in room 2. Above Room 2: A tiger is in this room. Above Room 3: A tiger is in room 1. The king tells you: The sign on the room with the lady is TRUE and at least one of the other signs is FALSE.  Answer the riddle, solve the sudoku, don't get eaten.  

Sudoku part (having noted the implications for the digits 1 and 9 from the riddle part above):
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Cells with a grey circle must contain an odd digit. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.  Cells separated by a black dot contain digits with a ratio of 1:2.  Not all dots are given.

If you'd like to try jovi_al's Negativity - an amazing new classic sudoku - then you can at the following link:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mdtTb9qmhp

title: A Serious GAS Attack
description:
Here are the URLs for today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 156 – Symmetric Unequal by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/we2zmjym 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits that are opposite each other (by 180° rotational symmetry around the center of the grid) must not be equal. 
GAS 157 – Symmetric Unequal by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/596xm5nz 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, digits which are in 180° rotationally symmetric positions about the centre of the grid must contain different digits.
GAS 158 Out with a Foot by Philip Newman
https://tinyurl.com/38xwp4w3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along green lines, neighboring digits must differ by at least 5.
GAS 159 – LK Killer by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/fftj5768 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage do not include repeats and must sum to the value indicated.  A clue outside the grid shows the sum of the indicated diagonal, which may include repeat digits.
 GAS 160 – XV Pairs Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/2efdhu78 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Two cells joined by a V sum to 5. Two cells joined by an X sum to 10. Not all Xs or Vs are necessarily given.

title: Sudoku Is No Longer Just About The Digits 1 to 9!
description:
*** Today's Sudoku***

Another masterpiece of originality today as Kit combines sudoku with the awesome Japanese pencil puzzle Heyawake.  This is SUCH a cool idea and it's executed beautifully. 

You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jQQf2DBMLT

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat in cages or along the main (marked) diagonals. Each cell in the grid must be shaded dark or light according to the following rules: 1) within cages, the dark cells will sum to the cage's total (if given); 2) dark cells may not be orthogonally adjacent to one another;  3) all the light cells must be orthogonally connected in a single group; 4) a straight (orthogonal) line of light cells cannot span across more than two cages; and 5) the dark cells along the two main diagonals must sum to the same total.

title: Red Light Green Light - Sudoku Squid Game
description:
▶ SUDOKU PAD - Our New App  ◀

It's just OUT on Windows via Steam here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1706870/Svens_SudokuPad/

You can now input your own classic sudoku puzzles into our software using our new App!  The app also comes with 12 handmade puzzles from us and we're also releasing occasional bonus puzzles too.  Already available on IOS and Android.

*** Today's Sudoku ***

This is an awesome take on the "Squid Game" Red Light Green Light from the Netflix series from Piatato.  It's such a clever implementation of the idea and SO much fun to solve.  Play the puzzle at the following link:
Version with flavour text rules: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8jPnpjrnr6

Version with plain rules:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hnrnDL7Q8L

Rules (flavour text version):
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given).  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The solver must run along an orthogonally connected path that starts and ends in the green cells. While on a green light, the solver must run as fast as they can and while on a red light they must try not to move. Speed is represented by the value of the digits! The solver is on a green light as long as the path goes on cells that aren't part of a killer cage. On these green cells the solver must keep up speed thus these cells must all contain high digits (6 or higher).  If the path crosses a killer cage, the solver has got a red light.  Here the solver must stay as still as they can in order not to be killed thus the red cells must contain low digits (4 or lower).  The path does not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally.

Rules (plain version):
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given).  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Find an orthogonally connected path that starts and ends in the green cells. Digits on the path that are inside killer cages must be low (4 or lower); cells on the path that are outside of killer cages must be high (6 or higher). The path does not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally.

*** More Patreon Content ***
Simon released a video on Patreon last week where he attempts the first 8 puzzles from the new Genuinely Approachable Pencil Puzzle series on Discord. title: Can You Keep Up With The Rules Changes In Sudoku?
description:
▶ SUDOKU PAD - Our New App  ◀

It's OUT on Windows (released yesterday!) via Steam here:

You can now input your own classic sudoku puzzles into our software using our new App!  The app also comes with 12 handmade puzzles from us and we're also releasing occasional bonus puzzles too.  Already available on IOS and Android.

*** Today's Sudoku ***

Today's sudoku is the 5th puzzle in a series of "Build Your Own" from the wonderful Joseph Nehme.  It's incredible how much can be done with just these small changes to the rules we know and love. This is definitely an approachable sudoku (genuinely!) so do give it a try if you have the time. Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JH8hqjFfD9

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The cages themselves must be deduced; each cage contains a "renban" that spans ALL of its cells.  The line must start at the killer cage sum clue and move horizontally and vertically through cells (but not diagonally).  The line must not branch.  NB As usual, the killer cage total must always be in the upper left corner of the cage (uppermost prioritised over leftmost). Cells connected by a "renban" line must contain consecutive digits in any order.  Cages may not overlap.

title: What Is A "Pencil Puzzle"?
description:
▶ SUDOKU PAD - Our New App  ◀

It's OUT on Windows (released two days ago!) via Steam here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1706870/Svens_SudokuPad/

You can now input your own classic sudoku puzzles into our software using our new App!  The app also comes with 12 handmade puzzles from us and we're also releasing occasional bonus puzzles too.  It's also available on IOS and Android too!

*** Today's Puzzles ***

Today Simon gets to try some of the Genuinely Approachable Pencil Puzzles published on the new channel "Daily Pencil Puzzle Discussion" on the Cracking The Cryptic Fan Discord server.  This channel publishes one new puzzle every day and they are an absolute treat.  You can join the Discord server here:
https://discord.gg/BbN89j5

This video includes 8 puzzles!  Can you beat Simon's times?  Each puzzle is linked below with its rules.  Enjoy (and please drop us a comment if you'd like to see more videos like this in the future ie perhaps a weekly video like Mark does with the Genuinely Approachable Sudokus).  If you do enjoy this video there is another with eight different puzzles available right now for our patrons on Patreon:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

Puzzle 1: Yosenabe by Freddie Hand

https://tinyurl.com/8yr6c26x

Rules: Move some circles so that every grey region contains at least one circle. Each circle must end up inside a grey region. A circle may move only in one straight line vertically or horizontally. Circles’ paths may not cross each other, other circles, or other circles’ starting points. If a grey region contains a clue, it represents the sum of the numbers in the circles which end up in that region.

Puzzle 2: Gems and Stones by Eric Fox

https://tinyurl.com/4tu6aa2a

Rules: Place circles into some cells of the grid - some white and some black - such that each row and column contains exactly one black circle. A cell may contain at most one circle. A clue outside the grid indicates the number of circles in the corresponding row or column up to and including its black circle, from the direction of the clue.

Puzzle 3: Aqre by shye

https://tinyurl.com/4rvsybx4

Rules: Shade some cells so that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Regions with numbers must contain the indicated amount of shaded cells. There may not exist a run of four or more consecutive shaded or unshaded(!!) cells horizontally or vertically anywhere in the grid.

Puzzle 4: Shakashaka by jovi_al

https://tinyurl.com/mryp3z3n

Rules: Shade a right triangle in some empty cells, each of which occupies exactly half the cell it’s in. Each unshaded area must be rectangular in shape. A number in a cell represents how many of the (up to) four cells orthogonally adjacent to the clue contain triangles.

Puzzle 5: Starbattle by Tyrgannus

https://tinyurl.com/yckjedwa

Rules: Place exactly as many stars is indicated above the puzzle in every row, column, and region. For this particular puzzle, this is 2 stars per row, column, and region. Stars cannot touch themselves orthogonally OR diagonally. For solvers more experienced in sudoku, this can be thought of as a king's move constraint !

Puzzle 6: Tapa by Freddie Hand

https://tinyurl.com/2p994t5t

Rules: Shade some cells so that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected area. Clues cannot be shaded, and represent the lengths of the blocks of consecutive shaded cells in the (up to) eight cells surrounding the clue. No 2x2 region may be entirely shaded.

Puzzle 7: Numbered Rooms by Eric Fox

https://f-puzzles.com/?id=yj72k5d8

Rules: Place a number from 1 to 5 into each cell so that each row and column contains each number with no repeats. A clue outside the grid represents what number appears in the Xth cell in the corresponding row or column from the direction of the clue, where X is the first number seen in the corresponding row or column from the direction of the clue.

Puzzle 8: Rassi Silai by shye

https://git.io/JXvXV

Rules: Within each region, thread a non-intersecting rope through the centers of all cells. No two cells in the grid containing endpoints of the ropes may touch each other, not even diagonally.

*** More Patreon Content ***

Also we've released a series of videos explaining the difficult puzzles in November's monthly reward:  The Japanese Sums Sudoku Hunt by Panthera and TheAsylm (including a video each by the authors!). title: GAS Guzzling
description:
Let's guzzle five more GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles! Here's where you can try them:
GAS 151 – Parity Lines by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/52p3w653 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on the same line have the same parity (that is, each line has all odd or all even digits.) Digits may repeat on a line as long as they follow sudoku rules.
GAS 152 – Parity Lines by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/d8v2898c 
Normal sudoku rules apply. For each grey line in the grid, either all of the digits on it are odd, or all of them are even.
GAS 153 Arrow by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/453d5w7y 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the value in the adjoining bulb (read as a two-digit number from left to right). 
GAS 154 – Difference by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/2d9kexjr 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If two cells are separated by a white dot, the digits in those cells must have a difference equal to the number in the dot.
GAS 155 – PAINKILLERS by Philip Newman
https://tinyurl.com/3pwesjdb
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat, and must sum to the total given. Digits along arrows must sum to the two digit total given in the corresponding pill, read left-to-right or top-to-bottom.

title: The Easy Version Of A Phistomefel Sudoku!?
description:
▶ SUDOKU PAD - Our New App  ◀

It's OUT on Windows TODAY via Steam here:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1706870/Svens_SudokuPad/

Check it out (and the bonus puzzle exclusively for SudokuPad we tweeted today on @crypticcracking).

*** Today's Sudoku ***

Today's sudoku comes from China and it's a slighly easier form of the livestream puzzle Simon attempted earlier in the week.  There is a ton of beautiful logic in this one:  Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6JBh99JDJJ

Rules: 
The grid must be divided into regions, each containing 9 cells.  Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9 once each. A number outside the grid gives the sum of the first M cells of the row/column from that direction.  M is the number of region borders in that row/column. The 4 cells surrounding a circle must belong to the same region. The 4 cells surrounding a black square belong to exactly three different regions. All unmarked 2x2 areas belong to two or four regions.

title: Supernova:  The Best Quad Sudoku Ever
description:
*** More Patreon Content ***
Simon released a video on Patreon on Tuesday where he attempts the first 8 puzzles from the new Genuinely Approachable Pencil Puzzle series on Discord.  These puzzles are awesome! You can join us on Patreon for as little as $2/month here:

Also we've released a series of videos explaining the difficult puzzles in November's monthly reward:  The Japanese Sums Sudoku Hunt by Panthera and TheAsylm (including a video each by the authors!).  Congratulations to RJ Powers for winning the hunt!

*** Today's Sudoku ***

Today's sudoku leaves us speechless.  It's called Supernova and it's by Nahileon.  This is a crazy, extraordinary puzzle that will leave you shaking your head in admiration.  Play the puzzle at the following link:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/MF3rQB3Tgr

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. A digit in a circle must appear in at least one of the four cells surrounding that circle. Every even digit must see at least one identical digit via a knight's move (in chess). E.g. if r5c2 is a 2 then there must be at least one 2 in r3c1, r3c3, r4c4, r6c4, r7c3 and r7c1.

title: A Sudoku Of Ice And Fire
description:
Today's sudoku is a tribute to the constructor grkles from his friend Playmaker6174.  It's called Fire Flower And Ice Flower and it's really rather brilliant.  Give it a try at the following link:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/RQQjRj3RPG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  The digit in the red cell (r1c1) is high [6,7,8 or 9].  The digit in the blue cell (r9c9) is low [1,2,3 or 4]. Digits along a purple line form a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can be in any order). Adjacent digits along a green line must have a difference of at least 5. A digit in a yellow cell must be greater than all of the orthogonally adjacent cells.

title: The Hardest Sudoku Of Them All: Simon Vs Phistomefel Live
description:
Simon attempted the new Phistomefel puzzle in a livestream.  It's fair to say this is one of the most extraordinary sudokus ever made.  

You can find the puzzle here with an example of how it works:

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0008A1

You can play the puzzle here:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fLtm97H9GD

Rules:
Every digit from 1 to 9 has to appear once in every row, column and region. 
The regions first need to be determined. Every region is a set of nine orthogonally connected cells.
A digit in a circle indicates the number of borders between regions it sees in its row and column. Note that the edge of the grid does not count toward this total.
Remark: There is no negative constraint regarding the circle, i.e. there can be uncircled cells containing a digit that equals the number of edges seen in the respective row and column.

title: It's a GAS Bag!
description:
GAS 146 – Breaking News by Philip Newman:https://tinyurl.com/caaj22mu 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey regions must also contain the digits from 1 to 9 without repeats.
GAS 147 – LK Clone by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/6m8tw8v4 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Shapes of the same color are clones of each other. All shapes of the same color must contain exactly the same digits in the same positions. No rotation or reflection allowed! Digits along a marked diagonal must sum to the value shown. 
GAS 148 – Between Sudoku by Sam: https://tinyurl.com/pr64cfvn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits placed on grey lines must be strictly between the two digits placed in the circles at either end of the line.
GAS 149a – Taonetonine by Mystery Setter #1:https://tinyurl.com/yd3ubtdp 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb. 
GAS 149b – Tatwotween by Mystery Setter #2:https://tinyurl.com/yj72w4yp 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Normal killer rules: Digits in cages cannot repeat, and must sum to the total given. Normal between line rules: Digits along a line must have values strictly between the values in the circles on the ends of that line.
GAS 149c – Tatrioine by Mystery Setter #3:https://tinyurl.com/7unyha4s 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits 1, 2, and 3 are indicated with (orange) circles, and the digits 4, 5, and 6 are indicated with (blue) squares
GAS 150 – GAS 101 – X-Sums by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/c5z53n4w 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding row or column, starting with the digit adjacent to the clue and continuing away from the clue, where X is the adjacent digit. For example: ?????7534 (19) would be a valid fill for a row where 19 is the sum of the rightmost 4 digits.

description:

title: The Light Bulb Sudoku
description:
Today's puzzle is a riddle and then a sudoku (and both are brilliant!).  It's called Light Bulb Moment by ZergreS and this is such an innovative idea, we're really blown away. You can play it at the following link:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JBNhmrn8dq

Rules: 
Riddle: A long hallway has 43 light bulbs on the ceiling. Each light bulb has a pull cord that turns it on and off. All the lightbulbs start turned off. 43 people go down this hallway. The first person pulls every cord: 1,2,3,4... (now all bulbs are on) The second person pulls every other cord: 2,4,6,8... The third person pulls every third cord: 3,6,9,12... And so on with the rest. Finally the 43rd person pulls cord 43. Which bulbs are on after all the people have passed through? Feel free to use the Sudoku Grid to work out the answer.  
Sudoku: Mark the final lit up bulbs in the Sudoku grid. (The hallway starts with Bulb 1 in R1C3) Lit hallway cells are brighter (higher) than their hallway neighbors. Hallway cells get darker (lower) as you get further away from a lit cell. Between every two lit cells in the hallway there will be a darkest (lowest) cell. It can be anywhere between the two lit cells. Arrows show the way through the hall. Digits along an arrow sum to the circled digit.

title: In GAS We Trust
description:
Here are the URLs for today's 5 Genuinely Approachable Sudoku (GAS) puzzles:
GAS 141 – Minmax Sudoku by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/4awj5kfu 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A value outside the grid gives the sum of the largest and smallest of the first three digits in that row or column, seen from that direction. For instance, if the first three digits in row 4 were 7 4 9, then the clue to the left of row 4 would be 13.
GAS 142 – Extra Regions by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/sykpryax 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each shaded region must contain the digits from 1-9 exactly once each.
GAS 143 Paired Pairs by Philip Newman
https://tinyurl.com/6stjwvnp 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Digits in cells separated by a black dot must have a 2:1 ratio. Digits in cells separated by an X must sum to 10. Digits in cells separated by a V must sum to 5.
GAS 144 – Big Bands Sudoku by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/5esprc2e
Normal sudoku rules apply.  The grey lines contain the following sequences, forwards or backwards (which sequence appears on which line is to be determined by the solver). 
1 3 5 6 4 7 8 
2 3 4 5 6 7 8
3 4 1 2 5 8 7
4 5 2 3 6 7 8
5 3 8 7 1 4 2
6 1 8 9 2 8 9 
GAS 145 – Thermo Quads by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/ru6hxppm
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits on thermometers must increase starting from the bulb. The four digits written on a white circle must appear in the four cells around the circle.

title: The Best Sudoku Puzzle Ever?  We Attempt THAT Puzzle!
description:
Here it is!  Simon's attempt to solve Two Truths And A Lie by zetamath.  The puzzle with a ruleset as lengthy as the puzzle is brilliant :) 

Note this puzzle originally appeared as a bonus video on our Patreon page (which is why the video introduction is as it is!).  You can support the channel on Patreon here:
https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

The rules to the puzzle are explained in detail below and you can play the puzzle here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/NFhHj2bQ2g

Rules:
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each of the following standard clue types occurs exactly three times in the grid: white dots, black dots, arrow, sandwich, Xs, Vs, thermos, quadruples, odds (grey circles), evens (grey squares), renban (purple) and German whispers (green). For each of those clue types, exactly two of the appearances of that clue are correct and the other is incorrect.  [A clue is incorrect if it is not fully correct.  Eg an incorrect quadruple might see one of the digits but not all of them.]

The "standard" clue types mentioned above are as follows:
White dots:  Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.
Black dots: Cells separated by a black dot must be in the ratio of 1:2 (so one digit must be double the other).
Arrow:  Digits on an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle.
Sandwich:  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column.
Xs:  Cells separated by an X must contain digits summing to 10.
Vs:  Cells separated by a V must contain digits summing to 5.
Thermos: Along a thermometer, digits must increase from the bulb end.
Quadruples: Digits in the small circles in the grid must appear at least once in every cell touched by the circle.
Odds:  Cells containing a grey circle must contain an odd digit.
Evens: Cells containing a grey square must contain an even digit.
Renban: Each purple line must contain a set of non-repeating consecutive digits (which can be in any order).
German Whispers: Adjacent digits on a green line must differ by at least 5.

title: The Real GAS Speedrun
description:
Here are the **CORRECTED*** URLs for today's puzzles:
GAS 136 – Killer Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://tinyurl.com/vtmf6tv3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a cage cannot repeat, and must sum to the total indicated in the corner of the cage.
GAS 137 – TOWTCBBAR by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/nasejkyv 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line must have values strictly between the values in the circles on the ends of that line. Additionally, digits along a line, including the circles, must form a set of consecutive digits with no repeats (in any order - for example, 1324 would be a valid order, but 1235 would not since it is missing a 4)

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the value in the adjoining arrow bulb, and may repeat as long as they follow sudoku rules.

title: Sudoku Rules Do Not Apply!
description:
Today's sudoku is NOT A SUDOKU!! This is a beautiful twist on the logic puzzle Fillomino from Mark Sweep (Frostini on Discord). Do let us know if you enjoy our occasional forays into the world of non-sudoku problems.  Watch out for Clover's reaction video to Simon's solve of her recent puzzle Everest on the channel tomorrow morning.  

You can play Chaos Fillomino at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gF94jrq8bf

If you prefer to solve Fillomino in Penpa then the link is here:
https://git.io/Ju4TY

Rules: 
Divide the grid into regions, such that no two regions of the same size touch orthogonally.  Each cell contains a digit that indicates the size of the polyomino it is in.  Clues outside the grid indicate the distance to the first seen highest digit in the corresponding row/column.  So, starting from a clue X, the Xth cell from that direction is the first appearance of the highest value in the row/column. Eg the 2 in row 2 means that r2c8 contains the highest digit in that row (although r2c1 to r2c7 may or may not have the same value.)

*** Two Truths And A Lie by zetamath ***
This puzzle is incredible, one of the best we've ever seen.  But it does contain an enormous ruleset - especially if the rules are fully explained. title: This Ghost is Very Sus
description:
Try Ghost Digit by James Sinclair here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rfj7QRQMRG 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages show their sums, and digits cannot repeat within a cage. On thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. But! One of the digits from 1-9 is a ghost, and is not bound by those constraints. The ghost digit still follows normal sudoku rules (appearing once in each row/column/box), but does not count toward cage sums, can repeat within a cage, and can appear anywhere on a thermometer (other digits on the thermometer must still increase from bulb to tip; the ghost digit is simply ignored).

title: A big problem with GAS
description:
Here are the five puzzles in today's video: 
GAS 126 – Odd Sum Pair by Cloverhttps://tinyurl.com/yn8r37hp Normal sudoku rules apply. Two digits separated by a small dot must sum to an odd value. Not all possible dots are necessarily given.
GAS 127 – Max Odd/Even Run by Sam Cappleman-Lyneshttps://tinyurl.com/3f7dc45z Normal sudoku rules apply. A number outside a row or column indicates the length of the longest run of sequential cells in that row or column which are either all odd or all even.
GAS 128 Eeeeevil Sudoku by Philip Newman (Clover)https://tinyurl.com/47jprf2s  Normal sudoku rules apply. MUAHAHAHA, and that's it!
GAS 129 – Kropki Pairs by Clover (Sam)https://tinyurl.com/35kat8h4 Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. Digits separated by a black dot must be in a 1:2 ratio. Digits not separated by a dot may be consecutive, in a 1:2 ratio, or neither.
GAS 130 – Making Lemonade by Sham Cappleman-Lynes (Philip)https://tinyurl.com/en5d3byw Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits around the (yellow highlighted) lemon shapes must sum to the total given in the two cells they surround (read left-to-right or top-to-bottom); digits may repeat on the same shape if allowed by other rules. All possible lemons may or may not be given.

title: A Burst of GAS
description:
Here are today's Genuinely Approachable Sudoku (GAS) puzzles:
GAS 121 – Gamma and Epsilon by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://tinyurl.com/yvtskrnb Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a black dot must have a ratio of 3. Digits separated by a white dot must have a difference of 5. There is no negative constraint.
GAS 122 – Nein Nines! by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/k4wfy4xv 
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 123 – BOGO by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/7nnmxze3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in a white circle must appear somewhere in the four cells surrounding that circle. 
GAS 124 – Extra Regions by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://tinyurl.com/9ydk2vy9 
Each of the grey regions must also contain the digits 1-9 exactly once each. 
GAS 125 – B1G3 Arrow by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/6rm7fj9n 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the circled total.
B1G3 Palindrome by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/85n3paay 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a grey line must form a palindrome (read the same from either direction).
B1G3 Renban by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/s36dxbma 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a purple line must form a set of consecutive digits with no repeats (in any order).
B1G3 Between Line by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/xx6pe5k2 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line must have values strictly between the values in the circles on the ends of that line.

description:
Peter Veenis (Sudoku's very own Pierre de Fermat) has scribbled in the margins of his notebook about a wonderful proof he has discovered that would help solvers understand his latest puzzle.  Can you prove Veenis' Latest Theorem and crack one of the greatest sudokus of all time?  You can play the puzzle at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/33MN2jT4Hf

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage (if given). Along each main diagonal (marked in blue) digits cannot repeat.  

*** Our Patreon - The Best Sudoku Club In The World *** 
You can join us on Patreon for as little as $2/month and access a lot of extra content.  Recent Patreon specials include Simon solving a Botaku sudoku (Euclidean Sudoku), the Lockout Lines Sudoku Hunt and Mark solving ridiculously hard cryptic crosswords.  Upcoming releases include a 45-puzzle Japanese Sum Sudoku Extravaganza from Panthera and TheAsylm where every puzzle creates a picture!

title: The "Empty Grid" Sudoku
description:
*** Join Simon at 10pm UK time tonight - 90 minutes after this video goes live - for his attempt at The Music Box Challenge in The Witness.  Link here:
https://youtu.be/HClxzvx1DQs

*****

We suspect you won't have seen a sudoku like today's ever before.  Not even The Miracle Sudoku was quite so sparse.  That's right Empty Grid by Jodawo literally has nothing in the grid at all.  What is going on?!?! You can play the puzzle at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/MLt47676Pr

Rules: 
In this puzzle ‘2-digit numbers’ read from left to right or downwards. Box 1 (NW) will contain all the 2-digit square numbers (16, 25, 36, 49, 64, and 81), which may overlap but must be entirely contained within the box. Box 9 (SE) is a clone of box 1, rotated through 180°. In each of boxes 3 (NE), 5 (centre) and 7 (SW), each digit will contribute to at least one 2-digit prime number contained within that box. Box 4 (W) is a magic square, with each row, column, and 3-digit diagonal summing to the same total. In each of box 6 (E) and 8 (S), the two 3-digit diagonals sum to the same number (NB box 6's number may be different from box 8's number).

*** Botaku Bonus Puzzle *** 
As mentioned in the video, we have a bonus puzzle today from the brilliant Botaku.  It's called Euclidean Sudoku!  You can play it at the link below and watch a video of Simon solving it on our Patreon page.

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

Play the puzzle here:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tMmgPBBP93
SudokuPad link: https://tinyurl.com/4t74y7rs

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Given two cells which both contain the digit N, the Euclidean distance between (the centres of) those cells must be at least √N times the sidelength of a single cell. In other words, if moving from one such cell to the other takes X horizontal steps and Y  vertical steps, then √(X^2 + Y^2) ≥ √N.

title: Playing Around With Parity
description:
***Thanks to everyone who has offered to help with our Google PlayStore issue (our Thermo Sudoku and Miracle Sudoku apps have been removed because they are too "repetitive").  We are hearing that, due to your effort, the decision may be overturned and we're keeping our fingers crossed.***

Today's puzzle is another original and brilliant sudoku from Dying Flutchman.  If you enjoy playing around with parity, you'll love this.  You can play the puzzle at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hTHqF2DP3b

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.   In the finished grid, every cell will be part of a group of orthogonally connected cells that share the same parity (ie an odd or even group comprising every orthogonally connected cell of the same parity).  Such a parity group can be as small as a single cell, or large enough to span multiple boxes and include repeating digits.  Corner clues give the sum of all cells in the parity group containing that cell.  Black dots separate cells with a 1:2 ratio.  Not all possible black dots are given.

title: One Of The Best Puzzles I've Ever Solved
description:
***Thanks to everyone who has offered to help with our Google PlayStore issue (our Thermo Sudoku and Miracle Sudoku apps have been removed because they are too "repetitive").  We hope someone at Google will see sense but it's not been resolved yet :( ***

Well, we are basically lost for words about today's puzzle.  It's called Triple Decker and it's by a new name to us: Mimaamakim.  It is simply extraordinary that this sudoku has a unique solution - let alone that it can be found by a human (if we class Simon as such...!)  You can play the puzzle at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Dm4HRqnL7p

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits along each line must be a set of consecutive digits in any order and must not repeat. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. Inequality signs point to the smaller digit of the two connected cells.

*** Botaku Bonus Puzzle *** 
As mentioned in the video, we have a bonus puzzle today from the brilliant Botaku.  It's called Euclidean Sudoku!  You can play it at the link below and watch a video of Simon solving it on our Patreon page.

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

Play the puzzle here:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tMmgPBBP93
SudokuPad link: https://tinyurl.com/4t74y7rs

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Given two cells which both contain the digit N, the Euclidean distance between (the centres of) those cells must be at least √N times the sidelength of a single cell. In other words, if moving from one such cell to the other takes X horizontal steps and Y  vertical steps, then √(X^2 + Y^2) ≥ √N.

title: If a River is a Snake, can it Touch Itself?
description:
Here's where you can try River Sudoku by Xailran: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/t9h6rqDj64 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A river is a snake path of orthogonally connected cells starting next to a cage; the digit in that cage shows the length of the river. The number in the top-left corner of the cage shows the sum of the digits along the river. Rivers must strictly decrease in digit value, starting from next to the cage. Rivers must not include cages. Rivers may touch themselves orthogonally, and rivers may overlap.

title: A Staggering Piece Of Logic
description:
Philip Newman's sudoku pack (mentioned in the video) is available to SudokuPad owners here:

https://sudokupad.svencodes.com/pack_countingto9  

You can also play the Philip's puzzles in other formats here:
https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*************************************************************************
Today's puzzle is a glorious hybrid puzzle of sudoku and the logic puzzle Cave.  It's by udukos and this is worth every minute you spend on it.  Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/H3Jt9J2fdg

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey squares are walls and green squares are cave.  Some of the cells must be coloured grey so that all grey cells (the walls) are orthogonally connected to the edge of the grid and all other (green) cells form an orthogonally connected area (the cave). A clue in the top left corner of a cell indicates the sum of the digits that are seen from this cell looking to the north, south, east and west. The cell with the clue counts once towards this sum.  Walls obstruct the view.  A cell with a clue must be part of the cave.  Within the field of vision of a clue, digits may not repeat.

There is an example puzzle available here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0007O3

title: The Eureka Sudoku
description:
Today's puzzle is surely one of the cleverest, most surprising puzzles we've ever showcased.  It doesn't look possible at all - in fact, it looks like it must be broken!  But this Hidden Thermo Sudoku by Prutsbeest is simply glorious. You won't want to miss this one! Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qF8D7mDRnF
Colour-blind friendly version: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rJHqfTTLDj

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.  The thermometers in this puzzle are all hidden, only their bulbs and/or their tips are given.  Corresponding tips and bulbs share the same colour.  For two thermometers only the tip is given (in grey and black).  All thermometers must be at least two cells long.  Thermometers cannot cross and different thermometers cannot share a cell.

Sam Cappleman-Lynes has made an extremely clever 6x6x6 set of puzzles.  We have released a solution video for this puzzle on Patreon and you can try to solve it yourself at these links (one to our software, one to penpa (which allows you to increase the size of the grids):

title: Sailing To The Sudoku Olympic Gold
description:
Philip Newman's sudoku pack (mentioned in yesterday's video) is available to SudokuPad owners here:

https://sudokupad.svencodes.com/pack_countingto9  

You can also play the Philip's puzzles in other formats here:

Today's puzzle has been recommended to us by our Discord server and it's another stunner.  It's called The Sailboat and it's Tom1i's tribute to Olympic Gold Medal winner Anne Marie Rindom.  Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6PtJf32R7L

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage forms a 1-width long line.  The sum of all centre cells along such a line is double the sum of the two cells at the ends of a line.  Eg 1 2345 6 is a legal cage since 2*(1+6) = 2+3+4+5.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage.

title: "The Witness" Sudoku
description:
We've just released Padlocked, an extraordinary Lockout Lines-themed Sudoku Hunt, on Patreon.  You can join us on Patreon here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic
($2 a month for puzzles, $3 a month for puzzles and solution videos).

Ricky Cruz does it again with his thematic take on the computer game The Witness.  This is just a magnificent sudoku and celebration of one of the great games!  Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/p9ttmLjQ4T

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Draw a path along the grey lines from the lower-left to the top-right that goes through all ⬡ cells. ⬡ cells indicate that the digits before and after them along the path have a 1:2 ratio. Red squares must be coloured depending on their odd/even parity. The path must separate the red cells such that all red cells in each region are the same colour.  It is NOT REQUIRED that red cells in adjacent regions be of different colour.

Sam Cappleman-Lynes has made an extremely clever 6x6x6 set of puzzles.  We have released a solution video for this puzzle on Patreon and you can try to solve it yourself at these links (one to our software, one to penpa (which allows you to increase the size of the grids):

title: The Sudoku With Zero Given Digits
description:
We've just released Padlocked, an extraordinary Lockout Lines-themed Sudoku Hunt, on Patreon.  You can join us on Patreon here:

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic
($2 a month for puzzles, $3 a month for puzzles and solution videos).

This week's puzzles have all seemed have virtually no information in them.  Today's really takes the biscuit.  RockyRoer's Sunflower has no digits, no cage totals and ambiguous kropki dots.  It's not likely to be easy :) Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mnPm37QtDd

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits in each cage sum to the same total, which must be deduced. Cells separated by an orange dot contain digits that are either consecutive or in a 1:2 ratio (or both).

Sam Cappleman-Lynes has made an extremely clever 6x6x6 set of puzzles.  We have released a solution video for this puzzle on Patreon and you can try to solve it yourself at these links (one to our software, one to penpa (which allows you to increase the size of the grids):

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bTBmNdrjdD
https://git.io/JuB3x

title: Literally Cooking ... with GAS
description:
Here are the URLs for the five GAS puzzles featured:
GAS 101 – Sum More Arrow by Philip Newman:
https://tinyurl.com/ywydf69s 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along arrows must sum to the number in the attached circle.
GAS 102 – O/E Thermo by Clover: 
https://tinyurl.com/35u229rn 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer increase, starting at the round bulb. Grey circles contain odd digits. Grey squares contain even digits. Thermometer bulbs are NOT necessarily odd.
GAS 103 – Thermo Clones by Sam: 
https://tinyurl.com/59m8wa4m  
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits placed on each thermometer shape must increase starting from the bulb. The four shaded cells are clones and must all contain the same value.
GAS 104 – Dead or Alive by Philip Newman:
https://tinyurl.com/3tf22cae
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cages cannot repeat, and must sum to the total given.
GAS 105 – Quad Max by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/22jhd43j 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A value in a white circle shows the largest digit that appears in the four cells surrounding that circle (digits may repeat around a white circle).

title: The Cube:  The Third Sudoku Dimension
description:

Today's video features a REALLY clever puzzle called Sudo-Cube by XeonRisq.  Not only is it beautiful but it's crammed with cunning logic.  Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7gbg37R9fj

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits on a grey line must be between the digits on that line's circled ends.  Digits on a purple line must be consecutive (in any order).  Adjacent digits on a green line must have a difference of 5 or more.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.  Digits can repeat along such a diagonal if allowed by other rules.

title: 400k Milestone
description:
Here's where you can solve 400k Milestone Medley by Olima: https://tinyurl.com/wnkh6k

Normal sudoku rules apply. The arrow outside the grid shows the sum of the indicated diagonal. Other clues outside the grid are the sum of digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 9 in that row/column. Grey circles show odd digits. White dots join consecutive digits. Digits on thermos increase from th ebulb. Digits on arrows sum to the number in the attached circle. Digits next to each other on the green line have a difference of at least 5. The purple line joins a set of consecutive digits, not necessarily in order. The cage shows its sum.

title: You Cannot Be Serious... The Phoenix
description:
No less than Phistomefel has been wowed by this extraordinary puzzle by apiyo.  It's called Phoenix Knights and you may well wonder how this sudoku can have a unique solution!! Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bGh8gpgMMd

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Neighbouring digits on a red line have a difference of at least 5. Cells separated by a black dot contain digits in a ratio of 1:2.  Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits. Not all possible dots are shown.

Sam Cappleman-Lynes has made an extremely clever 6x6x6 set of puzzles.  We have released a solution video for this puzzle on Patreon and you can try to solve it yourself at these links (one to our software, one to penpa (which allows you to increase the size of the grids):

title: Godzilla In Sudokutown
description:
FryTheGuy has created this awesome puzzle in which Godzilla lays waste to the skyscrapers of Sudokutown! Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4GP3nrFJLd

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey circles contain odd digits. Digits in the grid represent the height of skyscrapers.  Clues outside the grid indicate the number of visible skyscrapers in that row/column as seen from that vantage point. Draw Godzilla's path through the grid, which starts and ends in the grey cells.  Godzilla moves orthogonally between cells and his path cannot touch itself orthogonally or diagonally.  Cells on Godzilla's path do not count towards the skyscraper clues (Godzilla destroys the skyscrapers). Godzilla cannot go through cells containing the digit 9. (He is not powerful enough to destroy the tallest skyscrapers).

Sam Cappleman-Lynes has made an extremely clever 6x6x6 set of puzzles.  We have released a solution video for this puzzle on Patreon and you can try to solve it yourself at these links (one to our software, one to penpa (which allows you to increase the size of the grids):

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bTBmNdrjdD

title: The 400,000 Subscriber Puzzle
description:
Somewhat incredibly, Cracking The Cryptic looks to have reached 400,000 subscribers.  Thank you so much to all of you who've joined us on this journey.  Today's sudoku commemorates 400k and it's a quite beautiful puzzle by PjotrV. Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QTjg9tFG9r

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Cells separated by a white dot contain consecutive digits.  Not all white dots are given.  The grey line is a "Double Digit Thermometer" where it alternatives tens digits and units digits.  Starting at the bulb the double digits increase along the thermometer. All double digits added together sum to 400.  Digits along each purple line multiply to 400.  [NB Some people have questioned whether r3c2 should be counted twice in doing the multiplication.  It should NOT be.  It only counts once.]

Sam Cappleman-Lynes has made an extremely clever 6x6x6 set of puzzles.  We have released a solution video for this puzzle on Patreon and you can try to solve it yourself at these links (one to our software, one to penpa (which allows you to increase the size of the grids):

title: Hitting the GAS
description:
If you want to hit the GAS, here are today's Genuinely Approachable Sudoku puzzles:
GAS 96 – Odd-Even-Big-Small by Clover
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LLFnFB9TNG  
1-8 must be placed into each row, column and 2x4 box. Symbols outside the grid show that the first two digits seen in the corresponding row/column are either odd (1,3,5,7), even (2,4,6,8), big (5,6,7,8) or small (1,2,3,4).
GAS 97 – Odd/Even Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/48tf28tw 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on grey circles must be odd, and those on grey squares must be even.
GAS 98 Phortress by Philip Newman 
https://tinyurl.com/9e83sw4z 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in grey cells are greater than digits in orthogonally adjacent white cells.
GAS 99 – Sandwich Sudoku by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/273e5pwa 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid show the total of digits sandwiched in that row/column between the 1 and the 9.
GAS 100 – Palindrome Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/yjecn3hs  
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey lines are palindromes, so the digits placed on them must read the same in both directions.

title: Our Guarantee:  You Will Be Absolutely Stunned By This Puzzle
description:
Today we feature one of the best puzzles we have ever seen.  It's called Squares And Circles and it's a debut on the channel for Burning Curtains.  It makes Simon laugh in admiration of its genius.  Give it a try at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JfjF889L8d

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.  The digits in each cage sum to a square number (eg 0, 1, 4, 9...).  Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.  There are 9 hidden zeros in the grid, which count as 0 for the purposes of cage sums and white dots.  The hidden zeros appear once in each row, column and 3x3 box and consist of all the digits 1-9 once each.  Hidden zeros may not repeat within a cage. 

Sam Cappleman-Lynes has made an extremely clever 6x6x6 set of puzzles.  We have released a solution video for this puzzle on Patreon and you can try to solve it yourself at these links (one to our software, one to penpa (which allows you to increase the size of the grids):

description:

https://tinyurl.com/3akz5m2w
Normal sudoku rules apply. In each marked 2x2 box, the two digits on the top row multiply to give the two-digit number in the bottom row. 
GAS 92 – π-seas 5 by Philip Newman: 
https://tinyurl.com/cr424vtt
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 93 – Windoku by Clover: 
https://tinyurl.com/jr9a3hmw
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits 1 to 9 must each appear exactly once in each shaded region.
GAS 94 – Antiwindoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes:
https://tinyurl.com/h7ww53nw
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each shaded region contains exactly four distinct digits.

https://tinyurl.com/45by73fc
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a line must have values strictly between the values in the circles on the end of the line. Digits in a white circle must appear in the four surrounding cells (in any order).

description:

A few weeks ago two constructors (Tallcat and Riffclown) invented a new sudoku rule: Lockout Lines.  These puzzles have absolutely caught fire and today we try our first one.  It's called Trickling Down and it's by Mr. Menace.  Give it a try at the link below:

title: The Computer Programmer's Favourite Puzzle
description:
Today's puzzle is by one of the most popular setters we've featured on the channel - Clover - and it doesn't look like there can possibly be enough information for this sudoku to be solvable.  But... there is! You can play the puzzle at at the following link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/T4dMrNr2pF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in column 1 indicate the column in which the digit 1 appears in that row (e.g. if r4c1 is a 6, r4c6 is a 1). The same applies to columns 5 and 9, with the digits 5 and 9 respectively.  Each digit in the grid represents a skyscraper with a height corresponding to its value.  Taller skyscrapers block smaller skyscrapers from view. Clues outside the grid indicate how many skyscrapers can be seen, in total, when looking along that row or column from that direction. 

The classic sudoku pack mentioned in the video can be downloaded free from our Patreon page here:

title: Going Full GAS
description:
Here's where you can try the SEVEN puzzles in today's video - all Genuinely Approachable Sudoku (GAS):
GAS 86 – Thermo Quads by Cloverhttps://tinyurl.com/2srbw37j
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb. A number in a circle must appear in at least one of the surrounding four cells.
GAS 87 – Clone Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lyneshttps://tinyurl.com/ubmmmvd6
Normal sudoku rules apply. The three shaded shapes must contain exactly the same digits in the same places.
GAS 88 Part 1 – LK by Setter 1
https://tinyurl.com/yp8m5f5b 
1-6 appears in each row, column and box. Digits along a marked diagonal, which may include repeats, sum to the given number.
Part 2 – Sandwich by Setter 2
https://tinyurl.com/yfatnaye
1-6 appears in each row, column and box. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and the 6 in that row/column.
Part 3 – Next to 6 by Setter 3
https://tinyurl.com/7fpayyae
1-6 appears in each row, column and box. Clues outside the grid show all digits in that row/column that are adjacent to 6.
GAS 89 – Made Ya LK by Philip Newman 
https://tinyurl.com/8dbz4n6d
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a marked diagonal, which may include repeats, sum to the given number.
GAS 90 – Classic by Cloverhttps://tinyurl.com/zu6zwajs

title: More Gas in the Tank
description:
Please have a go at today's FIVE genuinely approachable sudoku puzzles here:
GAS 81 – Three-in-a-row by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: 
https://tinyurl.com/4ryej9xs  
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each marked line contains either three even digits or three odd digits.
GAS 82 – Triple Double by Philip Newman: 
https://tinyurl.com/sjjvewy4 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells connected by a black dot must have the ratio given.
GAS 83 – Even Sandwich by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/akbj9crm 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Whenever a digit is shown outside of a row or column, that digit must be ‘sandwiched’ between two even digits in that row or column. Not all ‘sandwiched’ digits are given.
GAS 84 – Even Sandwich by Sam Cappleman-Lynes:
https://tinyurl.com/9tr79ea4 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If a number is given outside the grid, then its two direct neighbours in the corresponding row or column must both be even. Not all ‘sandwiched’ digits are necessarily given. 
GAS 85: To Me, My … by Philip Newman
https://tinyurl.com/52fyfva3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are the sum of the first X digits in the corresponding row or column, starting from the digit adjacent to the clue and continuing away from the clue, where X is the adjacent digit.

title: Is This Puzzle Impossible?  Some Think So!
description:
Our book is very close to release - thanks to everyone who supported the Kickstarter.  If you still need to order it then you can do so here:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits

These brilliant constructors continue to surprise us with new ideas around familiar rulesets.  Today's sudoku is called Lattice and it's the work of DVFrank and it's magnificent.  And many of you have claimed it's impossible.  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3mg6PRM6bF

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The clue outside the grid gives the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.  Digits can repeat along this diagonal if allowed by other rules.

title: This Is NOT A Crossword!!
description:
Our book is very close to release - thanks to everyone who supported the Kickstarter.  If you still need to order it then you can do so here:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits

Today sees the return of Pentominous - a ruleset we love - to CtC!  This puzzle is by Elyot Grant and it's really clever - don't guess to solve it!!  The puzzle first appeared on gmpuzzles.com on 1 April but we detect no hint of April Fool about it!  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rf8N7NJRp3

Rules: 
Divide the white cells in the grid into pentominoes (five-cell regions) so that no two pentominoes of the same shape (including rotations/reflections) share an edge.

https://www.gmpuzzles.com/blog/2021/04/pentominous-by-elyot-grant/

title: A New Setter With Some Amazing Tricks
description:
Our book is very close to release - thanks to everyone who supported the Kickstarter.  If you still need to order it then you can do so here:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits

Xeonrisq is a new name to us but it's fair to say they are an amazing sudoku constructor - just on the basis of this one puzzle.  Do give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mhHB7J4P4p

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.  Digits can repeat along such a diagonal if allowed by other rules. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.  The digits in each cage, when added together, sum to the same total for each cage.

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Each line in the grid is one of the three types of line: Renban (a series of consecutive digits, including no repeats, appears on the line, not necessarily in order); Whisper (digits next to each other on the line must have a difference of at least 5); Palindrome (the line reads the same forwards and backwards). You must decide which lines have which property.

title: Turning on the Gas
description:
We turn on the GAS again with 5 Genuinely Approachable Sudokus. Here are the URLs:
GAS 71 – Slot Machine by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/n65xuz5d 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each blue stripe must contain the same sequence of digits. The sequence can start at any point on the stripe and wraps back around to the top of the stripe after reaching the bottom.
GAS 72 – Position Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/r39yats5
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid gives the position of the largest digit in the first three cells in the corresponding direction.
GAS 73 – Purple Haze by Philip Newman
https://tinyurl.com/57pnyyhm 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a purple line must form a set of consecutive digits with no repeats (on any order).
GAS 74 – Numbered Rooms by Clover 
https://tinyurl.com/bz2rt5eb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. If there is a digit beside a row or column, look at the first cell in that row/column. The value in that cell tells you where to place the outside digit in the row/column.

title: Is This SAT Sudoku Harder Than Actual SATs?!
description:
Our book is very close to release - thanks to everyone who supported the Kickstarter.  If you still need to order it then you can do so here:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits

Today's puzzle is an absolutely brilliant riff on the SAT exams from RockyRoer.  Can you answer the multiple choice questions correctly?!  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mFrFt2R4gr

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Each 3x3 box contains 4 ovals.  Exactly one oval is correct ie every digit in the oval must appear somewhere in the surrounding four cells.  The other three ovals are incorrect ie no digit from an incorrect oval can appear in any of the four cells surrounding that oval.
