GAS 66 – Coast to Coast by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://tinyurl.com/r7rz3fxt Normal sudoku rules apply. If two digits are given outside the grid, then they must appear (in either order) in symmetric positions in the first and last three cells of that row.
GAS 67 – Quad Wrangle by Philip Newman: https://tinyurl.com/fjkrhp72 Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in circles must appear in the four surrounding cells (in any order).
GAS 68 – X Thermo by Clover: https://tinyurl.com/49aj38x2 Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a thermometer, must increase, starting from the bulb. Digits separated by X must sum to 10. Not all X’s are necessarily given.
GAS 69 – Deficit Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes:https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/dnDqHDQNB8 Place 1-7 such that each row, column and outlined 6-cell region contains each number at most once. 
Surplus Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4dgGmtf6RQ Place 1-7 such that each row, column and outlined 8-cell region contains each number at least once. 
GAS 70: Did Set Join? By Philip Newmanhttps://tinyurl.com/8j376kjv Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot appear in the same relative position in different boxes.

title: One Of The World's Fastest Solvers Sets A Puzzle
description:
Our book is very close to release - thanks to everyone who supported the Kickstarter.  If you still need to order it then you can do so here:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits

Freddie Hand is one of the world's best puzzle solvers - it turns out he's also one of the world's best puzzle makers.  This is a Kakuro with some added Kropki and puzzles don't get much better than this.  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/9pnq68nq6m

Rules: 
Enter a single digit from 1 to 9 into each white cell so that the sum of digits in each Across entry equals the value in grey to the left of the entry (if given), and the sum of digits in each Down entry equals the value in grey above the entry (if given). No digit may be repeated within a single entry.  A white circle between two cells shows that the digits in those cells are consecutive (i.e., they differ by 1). A black circle shows that the digit in one of the cells has twice the value of the other. If there is no circle between adjacent cells, neither of these properties holds. (Note: between 1 and 2, either a white or a black circle can be given.) 

PS Thanks so much to everyone who joined Episode 5 of Simon attempting to play The Witness last night.  The next stream should be on Sunday evening at 10pm UK time.  We'll announce it on Twitter (@crypticcracking).

title: Your Snake MAY Touch Itself :)
description:
Our book is very close to release - thanks to everyone who supported the Kickstarter.  If you still need to order it then you can do so here:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits

A sudoku by Joseph Nehme that you have to build yourself - oh and there are snakes - what's not to love!!  Apologies for another long video but our mission is to showcase the very best puzzles in the world and this is one of them :) Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/nGtnmLtndn

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. The cages themselves must be deduced.  Each cage is a snake path of orthogonally connected cells that starts or ends at the cage sum cell.  Each cage is a minimum of 2 cells long.  Note the snake line must not branch; must always have the small cage total clue in its top left corner (topmost prioritised over leftmost); and your snake MAY touch itself.  Adjacent digits along each snake path must have a difference of at least 5. Cages may not overlap.

PS Episode 5 of Simon attempting to play The Witness is scheduled for Tuesday evening at 10pm UK time.  We'll announce it on Twitter (@crypticcracking).

description:
Here are today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles:
GAS 61 – Shhhh! by Philip Newman:
https://tinyurl.com/m9d5tn4 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along green lines, digits differ from their neighbours by at least 5.
GAS 62 – Arrow by Clover: 
https://tinyurl.com/bzeymea3 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the number in the attached circle, and may include repeats.
GAS 63 – Cupid Sudoku by Sam: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qMRg43pfRn
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on an arrow must repeat at least once in the direction of the arrow.
GAS 64 – GAS LXIV by Philip Newman:
https://tinyurl.com/rx2t57jk 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells separated by an X must sum to 10, and those in cells separated by a V must sum to 5. Not all Xs and Vs are given.
GAS 65 – X-Sums by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/ymmeadmb 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A clue outside the grid sums the first X digits in that row/column from that direction, where X is the first of those digits.

title: A Sudoku Marvel From The Multiverse
description:
Our book is very close to release - thanks to everyone who supported the Kickstarter.  If you still need to order it then you can do so here:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits

Ok so let's cut to the chase:  This puzzle is BRUTALLY difficult.  It may be called "2D Wave Particles" but you'll need to think in a lot of dimensions to solve it!!  It has burned through our testers and came to Simon with a great big warning about the likely length of video...  Will he be able to crack zetamath's masterpiece? Give the puzzle a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/F3NGgR7RnB

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  No two cells in the same position within a box can contain the same digits.  (Eg r1c4 and r7c7 must be different as both occupy the first cell of their boxes).  The cells separated by the black dot have a ratio of 2:1.  (Not all possible dots are given).  Digits on a purple line must be between the circled digits at the line's ends.  The upper right vertical line is an arrow.  The digit in that circle is the sum of the digits along the arrow.

PS Thanks to everyone who has joined Simon's livestreams of The Witness!  Episode 4 is planned for Thursday evening at 10pm UK time - we'll announce it on Twitter (@crypticcracking).

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a white dot must be consecutive. All dots may not be given.
GAS 57 – Outside Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/24ktt57x 
Normal sudoku rules apply. A digit outside the grid means that the digit appears in the first three cells in the corresponding direction.
GAS 58 – 129 Snowflake by Philip Newman
https://tinyurl.com/zdevva6w 
Normal sudoku rules apply. And that’s it!
GAS 59 – Creasing Sudoku by Clover 
https://tinyurl.com/43m73m9x 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along each line, digits must strictly increase or strictly decrease. The direction in which they increase must be determined by the solver.
GAS 60 – Round Off by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://tinyurl.com/pc8c2cw7 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each cage contains a two-digit number, read left-to-right or downwards. The result of rounding that number to the nearest 10 (5s round up) is written in the corner of the cage.

https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits

PLEASE NOTE:  The rules card on today's video is incorrect.  Apologies.  Too much editing of the intro/outro.  The rules for this puzzle will be correct at the puzzle link and are stated correctly below.

Today's sudoku is a tribute to Gene Roddenberry who would have been 100 years old today.  Gene created Star Trek, which first aired on US TV in 1966!  The puzzle is by Florian Wortmann and it's top-quality! Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/TrFhNFqBLT

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Arrowed clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits on the indicated diagonal.  The (unarrowed) 21 clue outside the grid is the sum of the digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in its column. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.  Not all possible white dots are given.

PS Thanks to everyone who joined us for Simon's stream playing The Witness on Tuesday.  Episode 3 is planned for Sunday evening at 10pm UK time. 

PPS If we manage to reach 400,000 subscribers then we'll be releasing a video where Mark and Simon answer community questions!  Please email us at crackingthecryptic@gmail.com if you have a good question for them :)

title: Come on, This is just Too Much
description:
Here's where you can play Too Much by Jonny Kaufman: https://tinyurl.com/nstvvkjc
FULL RULES: Normal sudoku rules apply. There are no negative constraints.
Box 1: Digits on the line are between the digits in the circles.
Box 2: Digits on an arrow sum to the number in the circle.
Box 3: DIgits in a cage sum to the given clue.
Box 4: A digit in a circle must appear in one of the four surrounding cells.
Box 5 is a magic square, with each row, column and 3-cell diagonal having the same sum.
Box 6: Two cells joined by a black dot have a 1:2 ratio.
Box 7: Digits joined by a V or X sum to 5 or 10 respectively.
Box 8: The digit in the marked cell is less than its orthogonal neighbours.
Box 9: Clues outside the grid show the sum of the indicated diagonals.

Rules:

title: GAS Guzzling - Genuinely Approachable Sudoku
description:
Here are today's 5 puzzles:
GAS 51 – Wheel Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4r2BpLTLNG 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The cells passed through by each wheel must contain the indicated values in the given order, but the wheels might have to be rotated into the correct position.
GAS 52 – Begun It Has by Philip Newman:
https://tinyurl.com/nk6ctb7w 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Blue/caged regions are clones of each other (must contain the same digits in the same order).
GAS 53 – Slow Thermo Sudoku by Clover
https://tinyurl.com/2rjfkdva 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a ‘slow thermometer’ must never decrease (starting from the bulb), but may repeat if they follow sudoku rules.
GAS 54 – C/L Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Q43b3PtDDR 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The two-digit numbers (reading left-to-right or downwards) either side of a C must sum to 100. The two-digit numbers either side of an L must sum to 50.
GAS 55 – Stroking my Ego by Philip Newman
https://tinyurl.com/strokemyego 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along thermometers must increase from the bulb.

title: The Miracle Puzzle
description:
Our book is real, as you'll see in the video.  We're so thrilled - thanks to everyone who supported the Kickstarter.  If you still need to order it then you can do so here:
https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/peterchayward/cracking-the-cryptics-greatest-hits

Today's sudoku is bonkers.  It's called Mediocrity (there is nothing mediocre about it) and it's by Fuxia.  And you will not believe it can be solved when you read the rules!! Have a go at it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Pm8N43nTMG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Some cells have an inequality sign next to an edge.  These inequality signs point to the smaller digit of the cells that share that edge.  Dominoes of the same colour are clones:  They have the same digits at the same position in the domino.  Cells connected by a white dot contain consecutive digits.  Not all possible white dots are given.

description:

title: More from the GAS Giants
description:
Today's five GAS (Genuinely Approachable Sudoku) puzzles can be played here:
GAS 41 – Clock Face Sudoku by Clover
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hdDrHHQM6B
Normal sudoku rules apply. Around a white dot digits ascend clockwise from a point to be determined. Around a black dot digits similarly ascend anti-clockwise.
GAS 42 – Renban Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gnTqBG79H8
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each marked line must contain a non-repeating set of consecutive digits, in any order.
GAS 43 – Personal Space by Philip Newman
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7dBBqHR3MP 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Orthogonally adjacent cells cannot contain consecutive digits.
GAS 44 – Irregular Sudoku by Clover 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hBgtTT8R8L 
1-9 appear in each row, column and marked region.
GAS 45 – Bent Diagonals Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/d2THtpfPJB
Normal sudoku rules apply. There are four “bent diagonals” in the grid which must each contain 1-9.

description:
BIG NEWS:  We have just reached 5,000 patrons on Patreon.  A huge thank you to everyone who is supporting us.  As a result we have released the Sudoku Murder Mystery Hunt FREE.  Just follow the link below and get cracking the crime!!!

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4pqQHjg6rG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. The inequality sign points to the lower digit. The green lines are 'palindrometers'. Digits along a palindrometer must increase from the bulb.  Digits along a palindrometer must also read the same forwards and backwards (like a palindrome) with the bulb acting as the centre of the palindrome.

Normal sudoku rules apply. Each arrow needs to be extended by one cell that is a king's move from its current tip.  Arrows cannot share their last missing cell. title: Simple Arithmetic And Simply Brilliant!
description:
BIG NEWS:  We have just reached 5,000 patrons on Patreon.  A huge thank you to everyone who is supporting us.  As a result we have released the Sudoku Murder Mystery Hunt FREE.  Just follow the link below and get cracking the crime!!!  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

If you like maths you'll love this puzzle.  This must be the most elegant use of simple arithmetic we've seen in a long time.  It's by Qodec and it's his tribute puzzle to his friend (and ours) clover!  Have a go at it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tmDnmJRL7m

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Some circles contain a maths operator (+,-,x,/). If you apply that operation to each pair of diagonal digits touching the circle then you'll get the number in the circle as the result BOTH times.  A circle with a ? instead of number indicates that the result is the same for both pairs of digits but must be deduced.  If a circle does not contain an operator, the digit(s) in the cirlce must appear in at least one of the cells touching the circle.

There are several examples illustrating the rules at this link:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0006YC

title: The Puzzle Of Rotational Symmetry
description:
BIG NEWS:  We have just reached 5,000 patrons on Patreon.  A huge thank you to everyone who is supporting us.  As a result we have released the Sudoku Murder Mystery Hunt FREE.  Just follow the link below and get cracking the crime!!!  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

Today's puzzle is an absolute gem from the brilliant Jesper Josefsson.  Ever wondered what a cross between spiral galaxies and fillomino might look like? No, neither had we!!  But this is a beautiful puzzle and you can give it a go at it at the link below: 

https://git.io/JGODG

Rules: 
Divide the grid into orthogonally connected regions. Each cell must contain a number equal to the number of cells in its region. No two regions of same size (ie containing the same number of cells) may share an edge.  Additionally, each region must be point symmetric, i.e. map onto itself if rotated 180 degrees around some point.

There is an example at this link, which is well worth a look before you attempt the puzzle:

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0006NE

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits with a ratio of 1:2. title: Another GAS Speedrun - days 31 to 35
description:
Here comes another speedrun attempt at 5 Genuinely Approachable Sudokus by Sam, Philip and Clover! Try the puzzles at these links:
GAS 31 – Near and Far by Philip Newman:https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/F4pq8732pq Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along a purple line must form a set of consecutive digits with no repeats (in any order). Along a green line, digits differ from their neighbors by at least 5.
GAS 32 – Mathrax by Clover: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qh9JfG47bJ Normal sudoku rules apply. Also, there are white circles in the grid that contain a number and a math operation. When that operation is applied to each of the diagonally opposite pairs of digits surrounding the circle, the result is always equal to the number in the circle.
GAS 33 – Palindromes Sudoku by Sam: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qB2PLPbq63 Normal sudoku rules apply. Grey lines are palindromes, reading the same each way.
GAS 34 – Ascending Order by Philip Newman:https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7b8G6LDQGH  Normal sudoku rules apply. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb.
GAS 35 – Arrow Sudoku by Cloverhttps://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/MRqgDj3MJR Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits along an arrow sum to the 2-digit number, written left-to-right, in the attached pill.

title: The Cube: A Sudoku Marvel
description:
BIG NEWS:  We have just reached 5,000 patrons on Patreon.  A huge thank you to everyone who is supporting us.  As a result we have released the Sudoku Murder Mystery Hunt FREE.  Just follow the link below and get cracking the crime!!!  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

**************************************************************

Today's sudoku is an absolute stunner by Marvin Kannhäuser called The Cube.  Not only does it look amazing but it's got a lovely (and approachable) logical path.  Do give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/m7mqTjNQb4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The digits in white circles must appear in at least one of the four cells touching the circle.  The digit in the grey cell must be higher than its four orthogonal neighbours.  Additionally every edge of the cube sums to the same two-digit number and this number is given in the grid by the 3 two-cell cages (all of which are filled identically), with the tens digit as the top number and the units digit below that.

title: 'Speed'running 7 GAS puzzles (slowly)!
description:
Mark takes on 5 more days' worth of Genuinely Approachable Sudoku - which is 7 puzzles this time! You can try them here:

GAS 26 – Antidiagonal Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/DgqqmmghFg 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Each marked diagonal contains only three distinct digits.
GAS 27 – Tilted Windmills by Philip Newman: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/nnrFQqJD3D   
Normal sudoku rules apply. Identical digits cannot be a knight's move apart..
GAS 28 – Thermo 6x6 Sudoku by?: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/gJNMrP2P4Q 
1-6 appear in each column, row and region. Along thermometers, digits increase from the bulb.
Kropki 6x6 Sudoku by?: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FrTbGnTHGt 
1-6 appear in each column, row and region. A white circle between two cells shows that the digits in those cells are consecutive; a black circle shows that the digit in one of the cells has twice the value of the other. Not all possible circles are given.
Killer 6x6 Sudoku by ?: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/P4LQDq6Nqt 
1-6 appear in each column, row and region. Digits cannot repeat in cages, which show their sums.
GAS 29 – Trio Sudoku by Clover:
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QHH2q4JDJ9  
Normal sudoku rules apply. 1/2/3 are marked by circles, 4/5/6 are marked by squares.
GAS 30 – Between Lines Killer Sudoku by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: 
https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/f6tJLF98b9 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits do not repeat in cages, which show their sums. A digit on a line must be somewhere between the digits in the circles on the end of the line.

title: Chaos Construction = Insane Sudoku
description:
*********************************************************************
BIG NEWS:  We have reached 5,000 patrons on Patreon this afternoon.  A huge thank you to everyone who is supporting us.  As a result we have released the Sudoku Murder Mystery Hunt FREE on Patreon.  Just follow the link below and get cracking the crime!!!  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

Today's sudoku from the video is yet another awesome puzzle by Jesper - it's called Chaos Construction: X Sums...  and it's quite magnificent.  Please have a go at it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3bJgQPpDdj

Rules: 
Divide the grid into nine orthogonally-connected regions, each containing nine cells.  Each row, column and region must contain the digits 1 to 9, once each.  A clue outside the grid indicates that the first X cells in the row/column from that direction are in the same region, with X being the digit in the first cell.  Moreover, the next cell (the (X+1)th cell) is part of a different region. The clue further indicates the sum of the digits in those X cells. In some cases, the clue has been replaced by a question mark, which stands for any single- or double-digit number. 

You can find an example puzzle at the following link:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0006Q0

title: Speedrunning five GAS puzzles (Genuinely Approachable Sudokus)
description:
SO … thanks to Movavi Support for providing a fast fix to my crashed editor problem, and here is today’s (yesterday’s) Sudoku Video after all!  Five Genuinely Approachable sudokus to try on these links:
Next to Nine by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/q9BrpGqTQM 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid give ALL digits that are adjacent to the 9 in that row/column.
House of X by Philip Newman: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qhRdqQDTq9
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits cannot repeat along marked diagonals.
Clone Sudoku by Clover: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jjmjLT7GqH
Normal sudoku rules apply. All regions of the same colour must contain the same digits in the same order.
Quadruples by Sam Cappleman-Lynes: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/M6drp6dh8g
Normal sudoku rules apply. Where a circle is given in the grid, the digits appearing in the circle must appear in the four cells surrounding the circle.
GAK by Philip Newman: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/fFfbTFNfL2 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in cells connected by a black dot must have a ratio of 2:1. Digits in cells connected by a white dot must be consecutive. All dots may not be given.
Have a great session!   Mark

Normal sudoku rules apply. description:

Today's sudoku was made by Aspartagcus as a tribute to his wife - they've been together for 11 years today!  And this is an incredible puzzle - it looks impossible but there is a way.... you can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/3GD4Fp9RGr

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.  Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in the ratio 1:2. Not all dots are given.  The red line is a palindrome for which the start cell and end cell must be determined.  The line must read the same in either direction.  Neighbouring digits along the line cannot be further apart in value than two steps (so a 5 would have to be next to 3,4,5,6 or 7).  For this purpose 1 and 9 are considered to be consecutive. (E.g., a 1 can have the digits 8, 9, 1, 2 or 3 as neighbours along the line.)

title: There are no Mistakes in Sudoku - just Rounding Errors
description:
Here's where you can try Eclectic Hoosier's Rounding Errors sudoku: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7NLb3Mj896   You'll love it even if you're not an accountant!

The Auditors prefer tidy sums, so when they got hold of my puzzle, they rounded all of my clues to the nearest five. Digits in cages cannot repeat, and they must sum to a total that will round to the clue in the top left corner. (e.g., 3, 4, 5, 6, and 7 round to 5, and 8, 9, 10, 11, and 12 round to 10, and so on.)  Digits on arrows sum to a total that has been rounded to the number in the circle, to the nearest five (where two arrows share a circle, they can have different (unrounded) sums.  Digits on the black dot are in a 1:2 ratio (precisely!).

*********************************************************************
Today's sudoku has been created by zetamath as a present for his husband, Tristan, on the occasion of their 10th wedding anniversary.  This is a brilliant and original puzzle. You can give it a try the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8P6Qq6QRpj

Rules: 
[If you are unsure about the rules below, please watch the introduction of the video where Simon goes through them in detail.]

Every row/column contains the digits 1-9 exactly once each. Digits may not repeat along the marked (blue) diagonal. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Every cage must be entirely shaded or unshaded, and every row and column contains at least one shaded cell.  In each row and column the cell that contains the number of shaded cells in that row/column is indicated either by a square or a circle.  Circles indicate that all shaded cells in that row/column are orthogonally connected; squares indicate those shaded cells are not all orthogonally connected (though some may be).  Whether a particular square/circle corresponds to its row/column (or both) is to be determined.

title: Creature Power!
description:
Here’s where you can try Creature Power! By Panthera: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jGj4Gf36nb 


Normal sudoku rules apply, and shading cells will help you solve the puzzle! Clues outside the grid show the sums of digits in shaded cells. The groups of shaded cells must be separated by at least 1 unshaded cell. In addition - one of the following rules applies: Rhino rule (cells that are n cells over and n+1 cells up cannot have the same digit for each value of n); Camel rule: identical cells cannot be an extended knight's move apart (a regular knight's move is 1:2 , a camel move is 1:3); Elephant rule (cells 1 or 2 steps diagonally apart cannot have an identical digit).

All rules are from : http://abstractstrategygames.blogspot.com/2010/10/fairy-chess.html

description:

[First apologies to Zombie Hunter - this video has the incorrect title and author in the video.  This is a problem with our video editing software that I now hope is resolved.]

Today's sudoku is a debut on the channel for Zombie Hunter and it's a heck of a puzzle.  If ever there was a puzzle that could act as a tutorial about the power of negative constraints this is it! You can give it a try the puzzle at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/F4ThRDdQRp

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid contains a 1-cell wide loop of orthogonally-connected cells.  The loop may touch itself diagonally but not orthogonally.  The digit in a cell with an arrow indicates how many loop cells are in the direction of the arrow (not counting the cell containing the arrow).  Arrow cells may be on the loop path.  All possible arrows are given (so if a cell could have an arrow it MUST have an arrow).  In cages, the small clue in the top left corner of the cage gives the sum of all cells in that cage that are on the loop path. Digits cannot repeat within a cage.

*********************************************************************
Today's sudoku is by the extraordinary TotallyNormalCat who set it apparently in just one hour as part of a speed-setting contest on Discord.  That doesn't mean it's easy to solve but this time the T'N'Cat does at least allow us to approach it carefully! You can give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mt7pgJhd9q

Rules: 
Totally normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits must not repeat in a cage. There is exactly one cage in the grid where the cage is broken ie either the sum is incorrect or digits are repeated or both.  The pink lines are "incomplete arrows".  The digit on one end of the line is the sum of the other digits on the same line.

title: Battle with a Sudoku
description:
Here’s Battleships Sudoku by Jeff Wajes: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/pGPJQ3B84P 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Black dots join cells with a 1:2 ratio; white dots join cells with consecutive digits. A 1/2 pair can be joined by a black or white dot. Not all dots are given.
Here’s where you can try Battleships Sudoku by Jeff Wajes: Normal sudoku rules applu. In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat within a cage. There are exactly five enemy ships. A ship is a straight line of orthogonally-connected cells; two ships are 3 cells long; and the remaining ships are of lengths 2, 4 & 5 cells. Cells in the given cages (green) are land. All other cells (blue) are sea. Ships can only occupt sea cells. Ships cannot touch each other, even diagonally. Each ship acts like a cage with a sum of 15. Shipd are unambiguous and the negative constraint applies. In other words, any line of 2/3/4/5 sea cells which sum to 15 MUST be a ship. Similarly any line of sea cells which cannot be a ship CANNOT sum to 15.

title: 100 Minutes Of Solitude:  The Fifth Movie
description:
▶ OUR NEW ARROW SUDOKU APP IS OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS!
Here are the links:
Steam:
https://store.steampowered.com/app/1613680/Arrow_Sudoku/
App Store:
https://apps.apple.com/us/app/arrow-sudoku/id1568407537
Google Play:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.StudioGoya.ArrowSudoku

*********************************************************************
Well we feared this might be a long one when we looked at the comments from Phistomefel's new puzzle Killomino - and, guess what, this is the longest sudoku solve we've ever attempted on the channel.  Will Simon solve it?  Give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/f4F3rNQBBr

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Divide the grid into different areas such that orthogonally adjacent areas contain different numbers of cells. Every cell is part of exactly one area.  Digits may not repeat within an area.  Numbers in the top left corner of cells are clues. An area can contain no clue, one clue or more than one clue.  All clues in an area must be identical and indicate the sum of the digits in that area.  [NB It is possible for two adjacent areas to sum up to the same total, as long as their size is different.]

There is an example puzzle that is worth looking at here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0006LY

title: Who Hid My Sandwiches?
description:
Here's where you can try Sandwich Capsules by RockyRoer: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Dh3pfFLfnJ 


Normal sudoku rules apply. Numbers in the circled cells represent sandwich clues. A horizontal capsule will be read left to right and tells the sum of the numbers between the 1 and 9 in that row. A vertical capsule is read top to bottom and indicates the sum of the cells between the 1 and 9 in that column. A single cell will be a sandwich clue in either its row or column, to be determined.

title: Better to be a Liar or a Killer?
description:
Here is where you can play Djmelee3000's Lying Mystery Killer in our software: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qH42fp9hLh 


Normal sudoku rules apply. Every cage in the grid will add up to the same total (to be determined), unless acted upon by a yellow cell. The yellow cells within or attached to killer cages indicate the amount the cage total is off by (eg if the total is 25 and the yellow cell is 5, then the real total is either 20 or 30). Digits in a cage will then add up to the new total, without repeats.  The black dots only help show which cages the yellow cells are attached to - they are not ratios. The yellow cell in r9c6 applies to the cage it is connected to, and possibly also its own cage.

description:

*********************************************************************
Today's video is the latest in our series of "how to set sudokus".  The constructor PjotrV - the pseudonym of Peter Veenis - has created this fascinating glimpse into how he created The Miracle Square Sudoku, which we featured on the channel recently.  

You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HP83P4q2Pr

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits in two cells separated by an X sum to 10.  Digits in two cells separated by a V sum to 5. For any pair of orthogonally adjacent cells where both cells are coloured yellow: The digits cannot add to 5 or 10; the digits cannot be consecutive (ie cannot have a difference of 1); and the digits cannot have a ratio of 1:2 (so one digit cannot be double the other).

NB There is no negative constraint re the Xs and Vs.  ie dominoes without an X, for example, can sum to 10 (or any other number).

title: Mahna Mahna.... Do Do.. Do Do Do.... Monomino...
description:
▶ OUR NEW ARROW SUDOKU APP IS OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1613680/Arrow_Sudoku/
App Store:

Google Play:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=com.StudioGoya.ArrowSudoku

*********************************************************************
Today's puzzle has been well-recommended and, having solved it, we concur with all those of you who rate it so highly.  It's called Ominoes and it's by PjotrV - who will appear in a bonus video tomorrow on how he set The Miracle Square sudoku!    You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/JGPFmGQqMT

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In the grid, every cell is part of an 'Omino', consisting of all 12 different Pentominoes, all 5 different Tetrominoes and 1 Monomino.  Ominoes cannot overlap and digits cannot repeat within an Omino.  The sum of the digits in each Omino must be divisible by the number of cells in that Omino.  The 1-cell cage clues each mark the leftmost cell of the top row of an Omino, and this Omino sums to the value of that clue.  The digits along a grey line form a sequence of consecutive digits but may appear in any order.  Each line cannot be part of more than one Omino.

title: These Snakes Are Touching Each Other!
description:

*********************************************************************
Today's puzzle is another gem from zetamath.  It's called Hydra and it's utterly brilliant.  You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/btgQm83JD2

Rules: 
Each row and column must contain the digits 1-9 exactly once, and there are nine orthogonally connected regions in the grid that also contain the digits 1-9.  Each region takes the form of a “friendly serpent”, which is one cell wide, 9 cells long, and does not touch itself, even diagonally.  Each serpent has a head and tail, also to be determined by the solver. Think of the head of the snake as its first cell, the next cell as the second, and so on.  A cell in the grid is circled if the digit it contains matches its position in its snake.  That is, the head is circled if it is a 1, and the tail is circled if it is a 9, and so on. ALL circles have been given.

title: One Of The Finest Puzzles We've Ever Seen
description:
▶ NEW PUZZLE/SUDOKU HUNT JUST RELEASED!!◀
We've just released a really amazing puzzle/sudoku hunt by Matyas Martinka. Any correct solution gets a shout-out on the channel!  We will be releasing a Murder Mystery Sudoku Hunt for everybody if we reach 5000 patrons.

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************
Today's puzzle has been recommended and requested in recent days by many of you.  It's also been described as "the best pencil puzzle I've ever solved" and various other stellar descriptions from some of the world's finest solvers.  It's by Gliperal and it's called Airlocks.  Simon attempts to solve it purely logically and concludes it might be almost immune to attack by bifurcation...  Is he right?  Do leave a comment if you manage to solve it about how you did it!!  

You can play it at the link below: 

https://test.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7tPnB8m9m3

NB If you want to use the "pen tool" Simon uses in the video then click the "cog" icon and select "Enable Pen Tool".  Then it should be pretty self-explanatory how it works :)

Rules: 
Divide the grid into pentominos (orthogonally connected 5-cell regions). Cells on either side of a given border must belong to different pentominos. Two pentominos of the same shape (including rotations and reflections) cannot share an edge.

If you prefer to use Penpa to solve the puzzle then here's the link:

https://git.io/JsZSD

title: "This Puzzle Is A Joy To Solve!" Says The Devil!
description:
▶ NEW PUZZLE/SUDOKU HUNT JUST RELEASED!!◀
We've just released a really amazing puzzle/sudoku hunt by Matyas Martinka. Any correct solution gets a shout-out on the channel!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************
Today we have another puzzle by Magnus Josefsson and what a gorgeous sudoku it is.  If you like pentominoes this will be heaven!  Phistomefel says "This puzzle is a joy to solve"!  You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/PB7bNLRffQ

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. There are 12 unmarked pentomino-shaped killer cages in the grid, one of each possible pentomino type.  The cages all have different sums and cannot have repeated digits. The cages cannot overlap with each other but may touch freely. A pentomino letter in the corner of a cell indicates that this cell is part of that pentomino cage. A clue outside the grid indicates that this diagonal has the same sum as that pentomino cage. Some of the clues have been replaced by "?", indicating an unknown letter.  Each pentomino cage has at most one clue of each type.
If you are in doubt about any of the rules, there is an example here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=000644

title: Do You Know These Simple Sudoku Tricks?
description:

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits may not repeat along the blue-marked main diagonals.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage. title: The Miracle Sudoku:  One Year On
description:
▶ NEW PUZZLE/SUDOKU HUNT JUST RELEASED!!◀
We've just released a really amazing puzzle/sudoku hunt by Matyas Martinka. Any correct solution gets a shout-out on the channel!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************
One year ago, we released a video we called The Miracle Sudoku.  It's a 25-min journey that starts with deep scepticism and ends in astonishment.   Mitchell Lee's incredible puzzle should perhaps have had more exposure but the YouTube algorithm never pushed the video.  Instead it's garnered nearly 3million views by "word of mouth" and "shares" on Twitter/Reddit/etc.  Thanks to all of you who've watched and enjoyed it!  

Today's puzzle shows where sudoku has moved in the last year.  It's a puzzle by Qodec, one of our very favourite constructors.  Just one given digit and a few lines in the grid...!  It's called 3etween and it's a joy from start to finish.  You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/BT7TMtM62j

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits on a line connecting two circles with black outlines must be between the digits in those circles. (I.e. the digit in one circle is greater than all digits on the line, while the digit in the other circle is smaller than all digits on the line.) Digits along an arrow in the grid must sum to the digit in that arrow's circle. 

Some comments have requested clarification on whether a digit can repeat on a Between Line.  The answer is yes (subject, of course, to normal sudoku rules!)

Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, shade some cells such that the clues outside the grid indicate the sums of the digits in contiguous blocks of shaded cells in the respective row or column. Normal sudoku rules apply. Apart from the central even cell, the grid must be filled with one or more pentominoes of each listed type, in which the top-left cell of the shape contains the given digit: 1=I, 2=W, 3=T, 4=L, 5=V, 6=X, 7=N, 8=Y, 9=P. Digits do not repeat in pentominoes, and two of the same type may not touch each other orthogonally. Cells joined by symbols are consecutive (white dot), have a ratio of 1:2 (black dot), or sum to five (V). Not all symbols are given.

title: Is This The Hardest Sudoku We've Ever Attempted?
description:
▶ NEW PUZZLE/SUDOKU HUNT JUST RELEASED!!◀
We've just released a really amazing puzzle/sudoku hunt by Matyas Martinka. Any correct solution gets a shout-out on the channel!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle... let's just say it's at least tricky!  It defeated every tester we sent it to but it came strongly recommended from the Discord server.  It marks a debut on the channel for Miky - the sudoku is called Sun Chariot and if you can find a logical path through it then give yourself a huge pat on the back.  You can play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/t9qDfPMm2p

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a single knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Digits along an arrow must sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle. Digits may repeat along an arrow if allowed by other rules. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cells sharing a black dot have a 1:2 ratio (and not all possible dots are given). Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal. The digits on a diagonal may repeat.

title: Don't Let This Snake Bite You!
description:
▶ NEW PUZZLE/SUDOKU HUNT JUST RELEASED!!◀
We've just released a really amazing puzzle/sudoku hunt by Matyas Martinka. Any correct solution gets a shout-out on the channel!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle has been requested/recommended several times over the last few days.  It's a quite beautiful snake-based sudoku by zetamath called Ouroboros.  You can play it at the link below. 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/67NL6D4jBH

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells must be shaded to form a single closed loop that is 1-cell wide. The loop may not touch itself, even diagonally. Within each cage, the sum of the shaded squares and the sum of the unshaded squares is equal. Digits must not repeat within a cage. The circles contain a digit equal to the number of adjacent cells that are part of the loop. This total includes the cell itself, the orthogonally adjacent squares, and the diagonally adjacent squares. Not all circles are given.

title: The Secret That Might Make You A Millionaire
description:
▶ NEW PUZZLE/SUDOKU HUNT JUST RELEASED!!◀
We've just released a really amazing puzzle/sudoku hunt by Matyas Martinka. Any correct solution gets a shout-out on the channel!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************
Thanks to RubikStevie for pointing out the tragedy at the start of today's video.  The Secret is important, as we keep telling you!  Today's puzzle is a Nurikabe LITS (!) by PolmanPoppins.  It may not be a sudoku but it'll give you just as much pleasure if you give it a chance.  You can play it at the link below. 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hg9FTjnfRm

Rules: 
Nurikabe: Shade some cells such that all shaded cells form one orthogonally connected region and there is no 2x2 block of shaded cells. Each unshaded cell is part of an island; each island contains exactly one number, which establishes how many cells are in the island.  A ? is a number of unknown size.  Two islands cannot touch, except diagonally. 
LITS: Shade one tetromino of cells in each region. Two tetrominoes of the same shape may not share a bold border, counting rotations and reflections as the same.

title: How To Set A Sudoku:  DiMono Explains
description:
We are thrilled to share with you this "builder" video in which DiMono explains the thought processes behind his wonderful sudoku Taco Bowl 3. Simon solved this on the channel a few days ago - link below.  Be aware this video contains SPOILERS so please have a go at the puzzle first if you can.  You can play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Fbf8q9pGJT

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, when two arrows face each other, they are crusts of a “sandwich”. Ie The digits in the crust cells must be the sum of the sandwich INCLUDING the crusts, in some order.   For example, if there are two arrows with 3 cells between them (→ _ _ _ ←), two valid solutions could be 74862 or 24867, because either way the digits = 7+4+8+6+2 = 27.

title: The "Miracle Square" Sudoku
description:
▶ NEW PUZZLE/SUDOKU HUNT INCOMING ◀
At the start of May we'll release a really amazing puzzle/sudoku hunt by Matyas Martinka.  First correct solution wins some merch.  Any correct solution gets a shout-out on the channel!

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle features a pretty incredible discovery by constructor Peter Veenis.  Can you figure out how a Miracle Square works?!  You can play it at the link below. 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HP83P4q2Pr

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits in two cells separated by an X sum to 10.  Digits in two cells separated by a V sum to 5. For any pair of orthogonally adjacent cells where both cells are coloured yellow: The digits cannot add to 5 or 10; the digits cannot be consecutive (ie cannot have a difference of 1); and the digits cannot have a ratio of 1:2 (so one digit cannot be double the other).

NB There is no negative constraint re the Xs and Vs.  ie dominoes without an X, for example, can sum to 10 (or any other number).

title: Ghost in the Machine
description:
Here's where you can play Ghost in the Machine by Pseudonum: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/HQfMPMGpj3
 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In each box, the digit that is the number of the box is a "ghost digit". There is only one ghost digit in each row and column of the grid. Digits in cages  must sum to the total given, except for ghost digits which count as zero. Digits cannot repeat inside cages, unless they are ghost digits. Digits along an arrow sum to the digit in that arrow's circle, except for ghost digits which count as zero. Every arrow contains exactly one ghost digit. Digits may repeat along arrows, if allowed by the other constraints.

title: Three Rings for the Elven Kings?
description:
This is where you can try Consecutive Rings by Qinlux: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Dpfp2Jt3tF 


Normal sudoku rules apply. There are three "rings" in the grid, or increasingly larger squares, with some breaks in them, represented by the yellow lines. Along these rings, digits must touch at least one other consecutive digit on the ring, except in the 'breaks' of the ring (where there is no line), where digits must not touch another digit consecutively on its ring. (so r1c4 can never be consecutive with either r1c3 or r1c5). These rules do not apply to cells on different rings that touch each other. Black dots show that the 2 joined cells have a 1:2 ratio, and not all possible black dots are given.

title: The Hardest "Easy Puzzle" Ever
description:

Today's puzzle looks so easy! How can a tiny kakuro hold us up for long?!  Well this is no ordinary kakuro.   It comes from the mind of one of the world's great puzzle creators Sam Cappleman-Lynes and one of testers couldn't place a single digit.  Give it a go at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/ddGfd499G7

Rules:
Enter a single digit from 1 to 9 into each white cell so that the sum of digits in each Across entry equals the clue to the left of the entry, and the sum of digits in each Down entry equals the clue given above the entry. No digit may be repeated within a single entry.

title: What Does An IQ Of 2,250 Look Like?
description:
▶  SIMON VS PHISTOMEFEL'S NEW PUZZLE◀
DiMono's solution video to Everything Wrogn Is On Fire is now available on Patreon for our $3 patrons and above.  All our patrons can also watch a new video of Simon attempting Phistomefel's new puzzle, Sisyphus! 

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's fantastic sudoku comes from an extraordinary collection of sudoku minds.  The puzzle is called Symmetry? and it has no less than 15 authors!  We believe it is mainly the work of Qodec but he also shye, Ben, xoned, abed hawila, Botaku, ahaupt, Hackiisan, Qinlux, Ethz, Philip Newman, Zack Szekely, Strosahl, Reverend and Gliperal!

You can play it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QnQHF7mpHG

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Each of the digits in the white circle must appear in one of the four cells surrounding the circle.  The green areas are clones. They contain identical digits in identical positions. The two purple cells are also clones and must contain the same digit. Digits in a cage cannot repeat and must sum to the small clue in the upper left corner of the cage. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb.  A black dot between two cells means that one of the digits in the cells is exactly double the other. Not all possible black dots are given. Cells with a grey circle must contain an odd digit. Cells with an grey square must contain an even digit.

Here's a link to Phistomefel's new puzzle Sisyphos (which Simon has attempted in a video on Patreon): 

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0005YM

title: Cylindrical Sudoku
description:
Here's where you can try Cylinder by Timothy Bexon: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Rhtd2M286j 


Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is a 'cylinder', continuous from the right edge to the left edge. In each row, certain cells that add to a given number are joined by a line. Any line in that row adds to the same number. The number increases, row by row, down the grid, and is shown in the blue cells in that row (a repeated number like 33 would be shown as a single digit (3), otherwise a 2-digit number reads left-to-right).

title: The Riemann Antithesis!
description:
▶  SIMON'S HACK FOR HARD CLASSIC SUDOKU◀
DiMono's Sequel to Everything Is Wrogn is now available to all our Patrons - we can't wait to read the comments!  You can find this and other goodies (like Simon's classic sudoku hack) here:

Today's sudoku has been set by Zetamath, who has passion for The Riemann Hypothesis (one of the "puzzles" you can earn a million dollars by solving).  Is this puzzle easier or harder than that, you can try it at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Rt2NJGtt7b

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits “sandwiched” between the 1 and the 9 in the respective row/column.  Cells along arrows sum to the digit in that arrow’s circle.  Digits can repeat along arrows if allowed by other rules.  X and y need to be deduced by the solver.  The row labelled "min" is the unique lowest sandwich sum across the entire grid.

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/jR4nn3qH92

Divide the grid along the dotted lines into pentominoes (five-cell orthogonally-connected regions) so that no two pentominoes of the same shape (including rotations/reflections) share an edge. title: Does The Computer Cheat At Solitaire?
description:
▶  SIMON'S HACK FOR HARD CLASSIC SUDOKU◀
DiMono's Sequel to Everything Is Wrogn is now available to all our Patrons - we can't wait to read the comments!  You can find this and other goodies here:  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle comes from the awesome intellect of Trevor Tao and it has a brilliant backstory!  You can find the spider solitaire game mentioned in the video, together with a link to Trevor's mathematical paper on it, below.  And, most importantly, you can try this lovely sudoku at this link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qNDr3fhnBJ

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. In each column, any cage of N≥2 cells must contain 
a run of N consecutive digits sorted in descending order, starting from the top. 
Negative constraints apply, e.g. 8 cannot be immediately above 7 unless both cells are in the same cage. 

Spider Solitaire Game: https://www.free-spider-solitaire.com/
(To get the instructions, follow the link, click More then click Help).

Trevor's paper on the computer cheating was published in 2019 in Parabola (UNSW, Sydney) and can be found here:
https://www.parabola.unsw.edu.au/2010-2019/volume-55-2019/issue-1/article/random-walks-application-detecting-bias-spider-solitaire

title: How To Make The Killer Confess
description:
▶  SIMON'S HACK FOR HARD CLASSIC SUDOKU◀
DiMono's Sequel to Everything Is Wrogn is now available to all our Patrons - we can't wait to read the comments!  You can find this and other goodies here:  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle is a gorgeous sudoku by Joseph Nehme... and you'll need to make this unusual killer confess the location of its cages!  It very nearly beats Simon too but why?!  You can give it a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/rm2JjMD2G2

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small total in the top left corner of the cage (ie the uppermost then leftmost cell). Digits cannot repeat inside cages. BUT the cage shapes themselves must be deduced! The cage can have any shape but the number of digits it contains must be equal to X where X is the digit in the cell containing the total. Cages may not overlap. Clues outside the grid show the sum of all the digits that are inside killer cages in that row or column. The inequality sign means that R3C4 is higher than R4C4.

Please follow us on Twitter: @crypticcracking

title: Simple Maths Tricks For Sudoku!
description:
▶  SIMON'S HACK FOR HARD CLASSIC SUDOKU◀
DiMono's sequel to Everything Is Wrogn is now available to all our Patrons - we can't wait to read the comments!  You can find this and other goodies here:  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle is by the ever-popular sudoku wizard Christoph Seeliger and it's not supposed to be too tricky.  What it is is wonderfully elegant and with a tiny bit of arithmetic you can get started quickly...  but can you finish?!  Give the puzzle a try at the link below: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GGrd2GTMLT

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. In cages, digits sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage.  In addition, each cage contains a standard "arrow" clue, which is hidden.  (In an arrow clue, cells along arrow must sum to the digit in the circle from which the arrow emerges.) The 'circle' part of the arrow will be at one end of the cage with the arrow extending along the cage all the way to the other end.  The circle may be any number of digits and multi-digit totals are read in the direction of the arrow.
[The rules will probably be pretty clear if you are familiar with arrow sudoku.  If not, watch Simon explain the rules at the start of the video before you try the puzzle.]

The puzzle was first published here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0005DY

Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a white dot must contain consecutive digits.  Cells separated by a black dot must contain digits in a ratio of 1:2. title: Super Crusty Sandwiches
description:
Here is where you can try Crusty Sums by Lucy Audrin: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/7dhpg42PrL 

Clues outside the grid give the sums of the digits that neighbour either the 1 or 9 in the row or column. The solver must determine which clues are for ones, and which are for nines. Where two clues appear, they give the sums for both the 1 and 9, and the order in which the sums appear (left to right in a row, top to bottom in a column). Where one clue apperas it could be for either the 1 or the 9. Some clues are replaced with question marks, which represent unknown numbers of any length. Equality and inequality signs give relationships between some pairs of clues.


Lucy's website is at: https://www.mindwielders.com/

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/FFQPhjnBrM

Normal sudoku rules apply. Additionally, there are some empty cages in the grid. title: Can You Handle This Rare Snake?!
description:
▶  NEW SUDOKU PUZZLE HUNT JUST OUT ◀
You can find our brand new sudoku hunt on Patreon now!  Can you unlock the secrets of the Wonders Of The World?!!  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle is just extremely clever and it's like three puzzles in one!  It's by python-master Peter C Hayward who calls it Star Python 2 - you can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mM7rgHLjHD

Rules: 
Sudoku rules apply ie place 1 to 9, once each, in every row/column/region. Additionally, the digits 1 and 9 may not be within a king's move (in chess) of themselves or each other. The final grid will contain a 1-cell-wide python, beginning at the given (red) 1. Each 1 and 9 in the grid will be part of the python. The python may not touch itself orthogonally or diagonally. Numbers in blue cells show how many of its 8 surrounding cells are python. Blue cells cannot be python. Not all possible blue cells are given.

Apologies to Peter for slipping an "e" into his surname instead of an "a" in the video.  This is the fault of my other friend Peter Heyward (yes, I know two) who annoyingly spells his surname the other way and I mix them up!

title: No Digits.  No Clues.  No Hope?!
description:
▶  NEW SUDOKU PUZZLE HUNT JUST OUT ◀
You can find our brand new sudoku hunt on Patreon now!  Can you unlock the secrets of the Wonders Of The World?!!  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle looks completely impossible!  It's by Mesmer and it's really rather wonderful.  You can try it yourself here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qTGfqrRLdd

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Digits cannot repeat in a cage.  The value of a cage is the sum of the digits it contains. The value of any cage must appear only ONCE on the board. Eg, if a cage value is determined to be 15, there is not another cage with the value 15. The inequality sign is pointing to the smaller digit of the two cells.  The cells on the diagonal pointed to by the arrow sum to double the value of the cage marked with X. Digits can repeat on the diagonal.

title: The Puzzle That Fools Simon
description:
▶  NEW SUDOKU PUZZLE HUNT JUST OUT ◀
You can find our brand new sudoku hunt on Patreon now!  Can you unlock the secrets of the Wonders Of The World?!!  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle is a beauty!  It was created by Cam Dennis and it fools Simon again and again.  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/74pnqPrLt2

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits may not repeat along each of the marked diagonals.  Cells separated by a "taxicab" distance of 4 may not contain the same digit.  A "taxicab" distance from cell A to cell B is the minimum possible distance from cell A to cell B when traversed only through orthogonal cells. In other words if two cells are H horizontal moves and V vertical moves away from each other, their taxicab distance from one another is H+V.

▶  SIMON VS PHISTOMEFEL ◀
If you'd like to try the Phistomefel's Yin-Yang Fillomino, you can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/49gg9R9jT6

title: A Staggering Puzzle Mash-Up
description:
▶  NEW SUDOKU PUZZLE HUNT JUST OUT ◀
You can find our brand new sudoku hunt on Patreon now!  Can you unlock the secrets of the Wonders Of The World?!!  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

*********************************************************************

Today's puzzle is another from one of the most popular constructors in the world, Jesper!  And it's a mash-up of two of our most requested puzzles types - Star Battle and Pentominous!!  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/2f4fTR6t6B

Rules: 
Place pentominoes in the grid, and stars within some squares of those pentominoes, so that all the following conditions are met: a) Exactly 2 stars appear in each row, in each column, and in each of the 12 standard pentomino types; b) Pentominoes must cover the whole grid, except the 4 central squares (shaded black); c) Two pentominoes of the same type may not share an edge (a rotation/reflection of a pentomino does not change its type); d) Stars may not be adjacent to each other (not even diagonally); e) Some borders between pentominoes are already given, and must be respected. Note that each individual pentomino can contain 0, 1 or 2 stars, as long as the total number of stars within all pentominoes of its type is exactly 2.

You can find a picture of all 12 pentominoes here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=00049Q

It's time to hit the arcade! In this grid, you need to take Frogger across the road and the river to reach one of the coloured frogs at the top of the screen.

In addition, there is an orthogonally-connected path starting at Frogger (R9C5) that collects all flies in the grid and ends at one of the colored frogs (small circles) in the first row. title: Creepy Crawlies really ARE scary!
description:
You can try Phil Preen's frightening sudoku here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/L9t3JF79Jd 

Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid show the sum of digits sandwiched between the 1 and 9 in that row/column. Some flies have got into some of these sandwiches. Each cell with a fly (Ѫ) is either 'sandwich filling' (included in the sandwich sum) or 'sandwich crust' (1 or 9) for one of the clued sandwiches. The grid also contains a couple of 'palindromic worms. The digits along the worms read the same starting at either end. Some of the clues have been replaced with letters. Each letter represents a different digit from 1-9.

title: The Final Boss Of Thermo Sudoku
description:
▶  NEW SUDOKU PUZZLE HUNT OUT TODAY ◀
You can find our brand new sudoku hunt on Patreon now!  Can you unlock the secrets of the ancient world?!!  

https://www.patreon.com/crackingthecryptic

Today's puzzle has been recommended to us several times over the last few days.  It's called The Tree and it marks a debut on the channel for the setter Garford.  This is a weird and wonderful sudoku and you can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6tnBLrmPgh

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The tree branches are populated by 2-digit numbers where the tens digit is placed before the units digit seen from the stem (ie the bulb in box 8) - in other words, tens and units digits are alternating along the lines.  The bulb includes the first number, read from left to right. The 2-digit numbers must increase along the branches. When a branch separates, the 2-digit numbers on all new branches must be greater than the 2-digit number on the preceding "parent branch". The 2-digit numbers must not repeat across the whole tree.

title: Only 1% Of People Can Spot The Genius Trick
description:
The thing about Cracking The Cryptic titles is that they sound like clickbait but they are actually true!  Today is Puzzle Day on the channel: First up, here is a puzzle we've had requested many times already - it's by Phistomefel and it's meant to be quite challenging.  Have a go and, if you get stuck, you can watch Simon's attempt on Patreon (link below)!  

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/49gg9R9jT6

Rules and example puzzle can be found here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=00053V

Today's puzzle featured in the video is a LITS puzzle by wormsofcan.  This is a really beautiful and classy puzzle and you can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/tH3hfpP4DQ

Rules: 
Shade exactly four connected cells in each outlined region, to form an L, I, T, or S tetromino, so that the following conditions are true: (1) All shaded cells are connected with each other; (2) No 2×2 group of cells can be entirely shaded black; (3) When two tetrominoes in adjacent regions share an edge, they must not be of the same type (L, I, T, or S), regardless of rotations or reflections.

This puzzle featured on the wonderful gmpuzzles, which you can find at the link below:

https://www.gmpuzzles.com/blog/

title: A Sudoku You'll Tell Your Grandchildren About
description:
Wow, oh wow.  This is a brand new puzzle by Jesper and it has blown our socks off.  One of our testers said "Puzzle Of The Year" and, although it's only February, it could be.  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/966jBbp2Hr

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small number in the top left corner of the cage (if given).  Digits in cages may not repeat. IN ALL CASES where two orthogonally adjacent digits sum to A or B, a dot is shown between them: ie White dot = Sum is always A; Black dot=Sum is always B; and Grey dot=Sum is A or B. A and B are different, and finding their values is part of the puzzle.

title: Did This Sudoku Make Us Cry?
description:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/BJRQ4DnFp3

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Cells separated by a knight’s move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit.  Digits on a line between two circles must lie between the circled ends (ie greater than the lower of the two circled digits and lower than the greater of the two circled digits).  The digits along an arrow add to the digit in the associated circled cell. Digits can repeat on the arrow if allowed by the other rules.

title: Extreme Sudoku: Simon Gets Duped!
description:
Today's brilliant puzzle is by tenaliraman and was recommended by one of our testers as a great puzzle for learning about the "Between Line" constraint.  What the So-and-So didn't reveal is that this puzzle is rated 5/5 for difficulty and also uses Disjoint Sets...!!!  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/QjJH8HpB3F

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cells in the same relative position with respect to a box cannot contain identical digits. (So eg, r1c1 and r4c4 cannot contain the same digit).  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.  Digits along such a diagonal may repeat if allowed by other rules. The digits along lines in the grid must be BETWEEN the two digits in that line’s circles (eg if the circles contained 2&7 then the digits on the line could only be from 3/4/5/6). Digits on the lines may repeat if allowed by other rules.

title: The Horse of your Dreams?
description:
Try to tame PjotrV's wild horse here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/BPBmFL4nfq


Rules:
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Also: 
- Digits along an arrow in the grid must sum to the digit in its circle. 
- Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. 
- The green line is a palindrome, it reads the same from both directions. Each different digit must appear at least once on the palindrome.
- The black dot means that the ratio of the two connected cells is 2.
- The white dot means that the difference of the two connected cells is 1.
- In cages, digits must sum to the small clue given in the top-left of the cage.
- There are no negative constraints.

title: The 3-Colour Sudoku Challenge
description:
Today's puzzle has been recommended by Mark (!) - it's called Snakes On A Plane and it's the work of Dying Flutchman.  Feel free to try the bonus challenge too...  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Dgtf7gGM4L

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grid is completely covered by 17 killer snakes! One snake of length 9, and two snakes each of length 1 through 8. A snake is 1 cell wide, and has exactly one single bend somewhere along its length (except the 1- and 2-length snakes). Numbers don't repeat within a snake. The nine given numbers in the corners give the total sum of digits in the snake that occupies that cell. These 'killer clues' apply to nine differently-sized snakes. Find the snakes and solve the sudoku.  

Bonus:  Complete the grid using only 3 colours.

title: Sudoku At The OK Corral
description:
Today's puzzle is really a joy to solve. It's by zetamath and you can play it here: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mr3fHnMfQp

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. You must shade some cells to satisfy all of the following rules: All shaded squares are orthogonally connected; no 2x2 region is entirely shaded or entirely unshaded; no group of unshaded cells is enclosed by shaded cells; clues outside the grid give the sum of the shaded cells in that row/column; all circled cells are shaded; and the digit in a circle matches the number of shaded cells within that box (counting itself). 

You can look at two examples which help explain the above ruleset here:

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?chlang=en&id=0005B4

title: Murder Mystery: The Sum Killer
description:
Today's puzzle is the new one by Joseph Nehme and it's not only beautiful to look at!  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/nFgHGGgPhD

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Clues outside the grid are X-Sums. Ie They represent the sum of the first X digits in the row/column where X is the first number along that row/column. 
In cages, digits sum to the total indicated in the top left corner of the cage. Digits cannot repeat in a cage but the killer cages themselves must be deduced by the solver!  
Each cage is in the same row or column as its associated X-Sum clue (colour coded for clarity). The cage can have any shape but its number of cells must be equal to X (ie X from its associated X-Sum clue). 
A killer cage total must always be at the top left corner of its cage and cages may not overlap.

title: Revenge of the Python
description:
Pit yourself against The Python by Ichtues here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/RR8mDPLDJJ 
 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. A 1-cell-wide python, which may not touch itself, even diagonally, begins and ends at the red squares. Digits on the python form a palindrome, with the purple square at the midpoint. The grey cells (stones) are NOT python. Each stone shows how many of its surrounding cells (INCLUDING the stone itself) are NOT python. All stone digits are different. The blue cells may be python. Each blue cell shows how many of its surrounding cells (INCLUDING the cell itself) are python. ALL possible coloured cells are given.

title: Why Hippos Are The Most Dangerous Animals On Earth...
description:
Today's puzzle is a beauty by Glum Hippo but be prepared to put your thinking caps on...  Hippos are dangerous!  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hngDFJtH92

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. Cages may not include repeated digits. Each cage should be treated as a “building” with a height equal to the sum of the digits in the cage.  (Eg a cage containing the digits 2, 6 & 8 would equate to a building of height 16.) Cells outside of cages are completely ignored for the purposes of the clues outside the grid. The clues outside the grid give the number of buildings that can be "seen" along that row or column, whereby (1) taller buildings obscure shorter buildings and (2) in a row/column with a clue outside the grid, there can never be two buildings of the same height. Note that a row/column without a clue does not necessarily have repeated building heights but may do.

[For those familiar with skyscraper logic puzzles, this ruleset above could be thought of as saying "it's skyscrapers but applied to CAGE TOTALS not cells".  (And subject to the restriction that buildings of the same height can never appear in a row/column with a cage-scraper clue.)]

Glum Hippo logo art by Miriam Martincic: https://www.miriamdraws.com/

title: Every Step In This Puzzle Seems Impossible!
description:
Today's puzzle was only published today and it's another by SudokuExplorer!  The rules looked so interesting that Simon decided to attempt it.  He must be mad.  You can play it here:

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Cages are subject to a Norinori colouring(!), as follows:  Shade exactly two cells in each cage; each shaded cell is orthogonally adjacent to exactly one other shaded cell; each shaded cell contains an odd digit.

You can see a NoriNori example at this link:

title: Snake On A Plane
description:
A 2D Plane!  Today we feature a puzzle from a brand new series by the constructor Greg Rodgers Powers who sets under the pseudonym Eggr.  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/dnHnLnTFQM

Rules: 
Draw a snake into the grid. ie a 1-cell wide path of orthogonally-connected cells, starting at the “head” and leading to the “tail”.  The snake never touches itself orthogonally but may touch diagonally.  (The snake never ‘doubles back’ to cover a 2x2 region.) All cells containing the same shape are 'clues' where the value in the cell denotes its “distance” from the head/tail. (Distance is measured as ‘number of orthogonal steps’.) The Square map points to the head of a snake. The Circle map points the tail of a snake. Each 'clue' also indicates how many of the 8 surrounding cells are part of the snake. Clues cannot be on the snake.

There is an example that's very helpful here:
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0004ZB

title: Shape Shifting Sudoku
description:
Try Zetamath’s exciting Kropkiesque Polyominoes here: https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/99mhp87F4G
 
Normal sudoku rules apply, and the grid divides fully into polyominos, each containing one circle and no repeated digits. The circle digit indicates the number of cells in that polyomino. White boxes separate adjacent, consecutive digits that share a polyomino. Black boxes separate adjacent numbers with a 1:2 ratio that are in different polyominos. All such boxes of both types are given. Three of the polyominos have been filled in, including the unique largest and the unique smallest.

title: Star Trek:  The Sudoku
description:

Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top-left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Grey circles can only contain odd digits.

title: Tata Steel Chess Sudoku
description:
Try Lizzy01’s timely Rook Sudoku here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/D8G844rT8p 

Normal Sudoku rules apply. Digits 1-4 are pawns, 5's are kings, 8's are rooks. Rooks can 'see' all cells orthogonally until their view is blocked by a pawn. Kings are not allowed to be seen by a rook from outside their own 3x3 box. Digits in grey cells act as clues, (those in column 1 for their row and those in row 1 for their column), indicating how many cells the rook in their row/column can see in total, including cells with pawns blocking its way, but not including the cell with the rook itself.

The puzzle on Logic Masters Germany: https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=0003XE

title: What Title Does This Puzzle Justice?
description:
Today's puzzle features a quite extraordinary sudoku by Qinlux.  It's called Self-titled Sudoku due to the Q, L and X in the grid and you can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/GQjmDB9rLj

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Each (marked) diagonal has the digits 1-9 once each.  Digits in cages sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage.  The blue cells in box 9 sum to 10.  The grey line forms a palindrome ie it should read the same backwards and forwards.  The three cells with grey squares in them contain even digits.  Clues outside the grid give the sum of the digits along the indicated diagonal.  Digits can repeat along these diagonals.

**************************************************************
You can play the classic sudoku "Pure Evil" by Sam Cappleman-Lynes at this link: 

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/hJdtjppq9F

description:

Normal sudoku rules apply. Digits in the first and second cell from the top and from the left are A and B. Clues outside the grid tell something about A and B: The clue closest to the grid gives the sum of A and B. The sum of the digits on positions A and B from that side is given in the clue in the grey bar.

title: A Puzzle That'll Make You GASP!
description:
Today's puzzle is one of the most unusual and brilliant we've seen.  It's by the constructor apiyo and it was quite challenging - at least for us!  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/Qm88j7J2dt

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply.  Cells separated by a knight's move (in chess) cannot contain the same digit. Grey circles and squares must contain odd and even digits respectively. Digits along a solid grey line must form a palindrome. Digits along arrows must sum to the total in their white circle. All of the digits 1 to 9 must appear on both main diagonals. The number outside the grid indicates the sum of the digits along its diagonal. Digits may repeat along the diagonal.
