title: The Inauguration Sudoku
description:
Try Figo Harr’s commemorative Inauguration Sudoku here: https://cracking-the-cryptic.web.app/sudoku/jjj2LdLLt8 

Normal sudoku rules apply, and digits increase along thermometers from the bulb to the end.
Clues outside the grid show the sum of the indicated diagonal. Every 4 must be orthogonally connected to a 6; however a 4 can never be next to a 6 in a thermo.


[The thermos follow the stripes of the flag and the top left ones are meant to incorporate the stars on the flag; the little killers are 1/20/21 - inauguration day, in American format. Joe Biden will be president #46, and first became a senator at age 30.]

title: World Sudoku Champion Tries To Stump You!
description:
[Pls excuse the slightly long intro - I couldn't bear to cut one of my favourite pieces.]

Today we're delighted to showcase the first "Sunday Stumper" from gmpuzzles!  This sudoku has been created by 3-time World Sudoku Champion Thomas Snyder and it's a beautiful puzzle.  The suggested times for solving are:  Grandmaster - 15mins (!); Master - 30mins; Expert - 60mins.  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/mRDtGNFGPq

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku Rules. The sum of the digits along the path of each arrow must equal the digit in the circled cell (digits can repeat on an arrow). Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end. The sum or product of the digits in each cage must be either 20 or 21.  The sum or product of the digits along the marked diagonals outside the grid must be either 20 or 21 (digits can repeat on a diagonal).

Check out gmpuzzles for daily handcrafted content:

title: WHAT Did 14 Geniuses Create?!
description:
Today's puzzle is a very special one - it's been created by no less than 14 of the world's great setters!  All is explained in the video but this is a sudoku you won't want to miss.  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/LNqP9d8tdj

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply. The grey circle is odd and the grey square is even. Digits along the blue line must be between the values at each end of that line. Digits along an arrow sum to the value in the associated circle. (The two-digit pill should be read as a two-digit number from left to right for these purposes.) Digits in a cage do not repeat; if a value is given for the cage, the digits sum to that value. Digits along a thermometer must increase from the bulb end. The orange cell is greater than the four digits orthogonally adjacent to it. Two cells separated by a black dot must have a 1:2 ratio. Digits along the marked brown diagonal may not repeat.

title: Cracking The Cryptic:  The Second Movie
description:
MAD. MAD. MAD.  These are the correct words with which to describe Undar Beyond's "Chaotic Wrogn" - undoubtedly one of the hardest puzzles we've ever tried to solve live.  It nearly breaks Simon - for which he apologises.  

You can play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6dP4FN27HB

Rules: (Yes, these are MAD!)

Normal sudoku rules apply but in the final grid, every clue is wrogn (aka invalid)... 
Clues are valid if: [Everything is "totally standard" Undar promises...]
-Digits in a killer cage sum up to the small clue in the top left of the cage;
-Clues outside the grid are correct X-sums.  ie Clues show the sum of the first X digits in that direction where X is the 1st digit.
 - Clues outside the grid are correct skyscraper clues.  ie The digits in the grid represent the "heights" of skyscrapers. Clues represent the number of skyscrapers seen from that direction. Taller skyscrapers block shorter ones.
-Digits on a thermometer increase from the bulb end
-Digits separated by a black dot has a ratio of 1:2
-Digits separated by a white dot are consecutive
-Digits separated by X have a sum of 10
-Digits separated by V have a sum of 5
-All digits in a circle appear in the 4 cells touching it
-Maximum cells are larger than all 4 adjacent cells

Not all clues are necessary and some of them are just there to "throw you off".

**************************************************************

description:
[3,333 patrons reached!  New puzzle hunt has been RELEASED on Patreon - see below for details!]

Today's puzzle is by Lucy Audrin and it's another gorgeous thermo sudoku - it's called Four Scissors for some reason ;)

You can play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/6dtFphTTqg

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Along thermometers digits must increase from the bulb end.  Digits in circles must appear in the four cells surrounding the circle.

BONUS VIDEO on Patreon:
Simon has released a bonus video on how to solve this Yajilin puzzle by Mitchell Lee (of Miracle Sudoku fame).  
https://puzz.link/p?yajilin/b/11/11/l0.a21a0.a0.a0.m0.a0.a0.a22a0.m41a0.a0.a0.a0.m0.a0.a12a0.a0.m0.a0.a0.a0.a0.l

Blacken some white cells and then draw a single closed loop (without intersections or crossings) through all remaining white cells. Blackened cells cannot share an edge with each other. Some cells are outlined and in grey and cannot be part of the loop. Numbered arrows in such cells indicate the total number of blackened cells that exist in that direction in the grid.

title: The Finish Of This Puzzle Will ASTONISH You!
description:
Today's puzzle is an old one!  In June 2014 Robert Vollmert released it on www.gmpuzzles.com/blog and we received a very strong recommendation to try it out all these years later!  The whole puzzle is excellent but the finish is extraordinary.  Enjoy!

You can play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8q4m4JMNnJ

Rules:  Chequered Fillomino 

The grid is to be divided into several areas, so that each cell contains a number that indicates the size of the associated area. Areas of the same size must not be vertically or horizontally adjacent. Given numbers can belong to the same area. There may also be areas without a given number. Also, it must be possible to shade some areas orange so that no bordering areas are the same colour.

title: Sudoku Karma
description:
Today's puzzle comes from Joseph Nehme and it's called Paintball Battle.  Simon would like to rechristen it 'Karma Police' Sudoku because, for a minute there, he almost lost himself!  This is NOT a totally straightforward puzzle :)

You can play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/bJBBGfdLtf

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  In cages, digits must sum to the small clue in the top left corner of the cage.  Digits cannot repeat within a cage. Black cells mean the ratio of the digits in the two connected cells is 1:2.  Not all dots are given.

BONUS VIDEO on Patreon:
Simon has released a bonus video on how to solve this Yajilin puzzle by Mitchell Lee (of Miracle Sudoku fame).  
https://puzz.link/p?yajilin/b/11/11/l0.a21a0.a0.a0.m0.a0.a0.a22a0.m41a0.a0.a0.a0.m0.a0.a12a0.a0.m0.a0.a0.a0.a0.l

Rules:
Blacken some white cells and then draw a single closed loop (without intersections or crossings) through all remaining white cells. Blackened cells cannot share an edge with each other. Some cells are outlined and in grey and cannot be part of the loop. Numbered arrows in such cells indicate the total number of blackened cells that exist in that direction in the grid.

title: 36 Cells In 36 Minutes
description:
Today's puzzle comes all the way from China and it's only a 6x6 sudoku...  it should be easy then... er no!  It is a really cool new type of sudoku variant and it's by Real Smile (Hong WeiHua) 真笑(洪卫华).  [Thanks to cdwg2000 for hosting the puzzle on his/her LogicMastersGermany page.]  PLEASE MAKE SURE TO CHECK OUT THE EXAMPLE SHOWN IN THE VIDEO (or at the link below) if you're unsure about the instructions!!

You can play the puzzle at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/4JrqrrjDTd

Rules: 
Normal sudoku rules apply.  Ie each row/column/region must contain the digits 1 to 6 once each.  Region shapes have to be deduced. The sum of the digits on either side of each region border are listed outside the grid in the correct order;  A white circle indicates that the surrounding 4 cells belong to the same region.  All possible outside clues have been given.  A "?" represents any positive integer. Not all white circles are given.  

https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=00053E

description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

*** OUR NEW KILLER SUDOKU APP IS JUST OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS - LINKS BELOW ***

Today's puzzle has been recommended to us by none-other than Phistomefel.  It's by Sam Knott, it's called Aquarium Sudoku and it is STUNNING.  You can play it here:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/8MrQmfqqp4

Rules: 
Normal sudoku sudoku rules apply (so 1-9 in each row, column, and marked region). Each region must be split into 'air' (green) and 'water' (blue) cells. (A region can be entirely one type.) All water cells must be below all air cells, and cells in the same row and region must be coloured the same. Additionally, in each region, the digits in water cells must all be larger than those in air cells. Each region has a different number of water cells, and all regions have at least one water cell. Along thermometers, digits must increase from the bulb end.

title: WHAT A Brilliant Sudoku!!
description:
▶Today's Puzzle◀

*** OUR NEW KILLER SUDOKU APP IS JUST OUT ON ALL PLATFORMS - LINKS BELOW ***

Today's puzzle is a really incredible new variant by Akash Jain (who constructs under the pseudonym udukos).  Akash was the co-author of Tracking The Cryptid, our recent Sudoku Hunt!  The rules are complex but they are well worth the effort. (If you've ever played the logic problem Nurikabe you'll find them very intuitive.)  You can play it at the link below:

https://app.crackingthecryptic.com/sudoku/qPBhLFBjPh

Rules: 
Normal Sudoku rules apply. Shade cells using the following rules: do not shade cells containing digits in their top left corner (“TLC”);  the digit in the cell with a number in its TLC gives the number of contiguous white cells in that area (i.e. it represents a Nurikabe clue); the number in the TLC also equals the sum of all the digits in that area; digits cannot repeat within a white area; no two different areas of white cells can share an edge (though they can touch at a point); the shaded cells are all orthogonally-connected BUT cannot occupy a 2x2 square (or larger); all the Nurikabe clues have been given. Note the inequality sign in the grid. Unlike in normal killer sudoku, the cell with the number in its TLC may not be the leftmost cell of the highest row of that white area.

The puzzle was published here (and the example is worth studying):
https://logic-masters.de/Raetselportal/Raetsel/zeigen.php?id=00050G

**************************************************************

We have released a brand new sudoku puzzle hunt for our patrons on Patreon!  This one has been made by Stéphane Bura and Akash Jain and it's awesome.  You can also find The Modern Art Sudoku Pack and a new sudoku from Mark:
